text: Introducing Auquan’s Credit Agent: The first autonomous AI for credit analysis and monitoring | Auquan Solutions Company Careers Insights Sign In Get a Demo ← All insights September 17, 2025 Introducing Auquan’s Credit Agent: The first autonomous AI for credit analysis and monitoring Introducing Auquan’s Credit Agent: The first autonomous AI for credit analysis and monitoring Jalaj Jain Company News Product & Technology Today, we’re announcing the launch of our newest AI agent: the Credit Agent. This is the first and only AI agent that autonomously completes entire credit analysis and monitoring workflows to provide a comprehensive evaluation of lending opportunities and borrower performance. Unlike any other AI tools that merely assist analysts with research and summarization tasks, Auquan’s AI agents independently execute workflows end-to-end, from data gathering through structured reporting, freeing professionals to focus on high-value work. With Credit Agent, we’re not just making credit work faster; we’re transforming how it gets done, giving teams the power to scale their impact without sacrificing depth or rigor. The need for a Credit Agent Over the past decade, private credit has ballooned into a multi-trillion-dollar asset class, fueled by institutional investors hunting for yield and companies seeking flexible alternatives to traditional bank financing. But while the capital has scaled, the workflows behind evaluating, monitoring, and managing these deals have not. Credit analysts remain under pressure to process ever more opportunities with fewer resources, all while maintaining rigor and compliance. At Auquan, we’ve seen the strain first-hand. Analysts tell us they spend three to five days on a single opportunity, combing through data rooms, normalizing financials, chasing market context, and drafting memos. Up to 80% of that time is swallowed by repetitive data wrangling, leaving little room for the strategic analysis and judgment that actually drive returns. The release of Auquan’s Credit Agent will revolutionize the way analysts work. With this innovation, credit teams can rely on a single agent to deliver a comprehensive evaluation of lending opportunities while continuously monitoring borrower performance. How does a Credit Agent work in practice? Here’s what credit teams get out of the box: Deal Screening: Instantly evaluate opportunities against lending criteria, highlight red flags, and deliver high-level analysis. Borrower Assessment: Conduct complete financial health checks, analyzing liquidity, leverage, cash flow coverage, and trends over time. Market Intelligence: Quantify sector-specific risks, analyze competitive positioning, and surface relevant market dynamics. Structure Analysis: Benchmark loan terms against comparable deals, assess structural protections, and highlight risks. Credit Memo Generation: Produce fully formatted memos tailored to a firm’s templates and standards and ready for committee review. Portfolio Monitoring: Continuously track borrower performance, covenant compliance, and market signals to surface early warnings. Regulatory & LP Reporting: Generate standardized, accurate reports for regulators and limited partners, removing manual reporting headaches. Together, these capabilities allow credit teams to replace days of manual effort with a single, seamless workflow. Breaking down the data silos with comprehensive coverage Credit teams can use Auquan to analyze proprietary internal datasets and secure data room information alongside public and subscription market data within a unified analytical framework. This comprehensive approach eliminates analytical silos and provides a complete picture that competitors cannot match, allowing for more nuanced risk assessment and opportunity identification in the private credit landscape. Auquan processes information on any private and public company worldwide, with new company coverage added on demand within one hour. This unmatched coverage continuously draws from more than two million data sources originating in more than 76 languages, including: Corporate filings and disclosures Financial statements and presentations Regulatory documents and legal filings News and media coverage (global, local, and industry-specific) Industry analyses and reports Specialized subscription datasets Overall, credit teams get a unified view with the depth and breadth of insight they need to evaluate opportunities confidently. The track record of proven success This announcement builds on the company’s proven track record of helping teams transform complex, knowledge-intensive workflows. Since its launch in late 2023, the company’s agentic AI platform has saved customers collectively more than 50,000 hours of manual work, empowering professionals across private equity, private credit, asset management, and other institutional investment firms to focus on fulfilling and high-impact work. A European bank with 2,700 active credits uses Auquan to transform what was previously a week-long portfolio review process into a 10-minute task. A top 20 global bank saves 1-2 days per borrower memo, while private credit teams can evaluate 2-3x more deals without adding headcount, maintaining thorough analysis while drastically accelerating timelines. Auquan’s customers realize immediate value through turnkey solutions while supporting custom implementations for unique research and reporting requirements. Already, 40% of the top 20 global financial institutions, including MetLife, T. Rowe Price, and Capital Group, trust Auquan to power mission-critical workflows across credit, equity research, risk monitoring, compliance, and sustainability. Available now The Auquan Credit Agent is available immediately, through direct purchase or the Microsoft Azure Marketplace . Credit teams can begin saving hours of manual work within days and unlock the capacity to evaluate more deals, monitor more borrowers, and deliver more impact without compromise. MGAs and insurers to process broker submissions in any format AI-powered tool enables MGAs and insurers to handle more quotes, boost sales, improve data quality, reduce servicing costs, and accelerate processing time. 5 December 2024: Insly , the low-code software provider to the insurance industry, has launched its first AI-powered solution, FormFlow , which removes a critical bottleneck in the relationship between MGAs, insurers, and their broker partners. The new tool, built following customer demand, captures data submitted by brokers in any format so it can be processed by quote and bind systems. This eliminates the need to re-key data, enabling MGAs and insurers to fulfill a higher volume of quotes, faster. MGAs and insurers rely on brokers to distribute their products, however, a bottleneck exists where brokers must either fill out quote forms for multiple MGAs and insurers or send risk details v ia email and document attachments. If they opt for the latter, it falls on underwriters to re-key the data, which is time-consuming, costly, prone to manual error and delays the quote process. In many cases, the cost and time required for MGAs and insurers to process numerous email submissions means many slip through the cracks. Insly estimates that underwriting teams currently handle only 30 to 50% of broker submissions, leading to a substantial loss of potential sales, and damage to broker and customer relationships. FormFlow removes this bottleneck by enabling brokers to submit risk details in any language and format, including PDFs, images, emails, or even handwritten text. The AI tool uses a combination of AI systems to extract information from broker documents and then map this into MGA and insurer templates, augmenting where possible with third-party data online. The system upholds the highest data security and privacy standards, ensuring each client’s data remains separate and secure. Insly estimates that used alone, Formflow can increase the proportion of quotes processed by MGAs and insurers to between 60 and 70%, and when used alongside an automated underwriting system this number could rise to 80 to 90%. It also reduces quote processing from days to minutes, and by augmenting with third-party data, increases the volume and quality of data for insurance underwriting by at least 10 times. “MGAs and insurers are losing out on a significant volume of potential sales due to a data-processing challenge,” comments Risto Rossar, CEO and Founder of Insly. “Our Insly Innovation Lab has been researching and testing the best uses for AI in insurance processes and this is an area where the technology adds huge value. “The tool we’ve created removes a huge cause of inefficiency, helping brokers and underwriters to collaborate more effectively, and aiding customers in sourcing the best cover for their needs. We’re excited to put FormFlow to work with existing and new customers, helping MGAs and insurers maximise their broker relationships and accelerate sales.” FormFlow can be used with any IT system, or where an MGA or insurer has no software, it adds value through digitising customer information in a structured format, augmenting it with third-party data for fast, efficient underwriting. ENDS For further information, please contact: Anna King About Insly Since 2013, Insly has been on a mission to help MGAs and insurance companies deliver better products, service, and profitability through flexible low-code software. Founded by Risto Rossar, who established the first digital insurance broker in the world in 2000, Insly is built on deep insurance and technology expertise, with products designed around the exact needs of MGAs and insurers. Fast to implement, Insly’s modular solutions span the entire insurance lifecycle, enabling MGAs and insurers to build a system that fits their evolving needs, while integrating seamlessly through open APIs. Improved workflows and automation mean Insly customers can handle on average double the gross written premium (GWP) as with their previous systems while gaining business visibility and insights to take their business to the next level. This is where the Type-C USB has started to step in, with more and more pieces of tech coming with a Type-C charger rather than the old favourite. So the question is why? If the old micro USB isn’t broken then why ‘fix’ it? ﻿ The New UKCA (UK Conformity Assessed) Marking By Ben Winstanley • December 15, 2020 The UKCA (UK Conformity Assessed) marking is a new UK product marking that will be used for goods being placed on the market in Great Britain (England, Wales and Scotland). It covers most goods which previously required the CE marking. What is MDR? The New Medical Device Regulation By Ben Winstanley • October 29, 2020 What is MDR? Medical Device Regulation MDR is a new regulation issued by the European Parliament and the council of medical devices. It is replacing previous medical device directives 90/385/EEC and 93/42/EEC. The requirements of the new regulation are more complex than previously and are different per product. The vast majority of products are subject to new labelling and documentation requirements, such as; • Requirements for a unique device identification number (UDI) • Traceability of products The new requirements specified by the MDR cover each role played by differing companies on the supply chain, meaning at each step there are new responsibilities to be aware of. When does the MDR come into play? The MDR was initially due to begin the transition in May of this year but due to the global pandemic it is has been postponed to 26th May 2021. This transition deadline has to be met by all companies and suppliers by the date. What does MDR mean for power supplies? IEC 62368-1 The new standard for ICT and AV equipment. By Ben Winstanley • October 27, 2020 From December 20, 2020, the IEC 62368-1 is set to take over from the IEC 60950-1 and IEC 60065 for the new standard for ICT and AV equipment. It brings together two separate standards linking terminologies and key engineering tenets, this new standard will become law and be used throughout Europe and USA. In Europe, the transition will be rapid and the expectation for all equipment to meet these new standards will be expected. Whereas, in the USA the transition will be slower starting with new submissions matching the standards and some existing products not having to be re-reviewed. Why the change? The IEC 62368-1 is a unified and smoother set of standards to follow internationally. It is here to revolutionise the approach for basic hazard safety, as new types of affordable products have emerged for use both leisurely and for business. Due to the constant changing state and technological advances blurs the lines between AV and ICT are blurred meaning the standards should begin to overlap Why Electric, Why Now? By Ben Winstanley • August 24, 2020 In a best effort to reduce our carbon footprint within the UK we are aiming to ban the sale and production of diesel, petrol, hybrid, and plug-in hybrid cars. Due to this, consumers will only be able to buy vehicles that run on electricity or hydrogen. Just under 1/3 of our carbon emissions in the UK come from transport, whether that be personal or public. By removing the public’s access to cars that can produce emissions the government can control the public transport and how energy efficient that is. There are already several electric bus companies including some in our own area. The Law Since 2009 the previous government started to get the wheels turning on electric vehicles becoming the norm. However, the real impact came from the announcement of a legal ban on all non-electric or hydrogen cars being created from 2035, which had been moved forward from 2040. This does not mean you will have to get rid of your petrol car, but it does mean that any car you wish to purchase from this point will be electric Differences between a Power Supply and a Charger By Ben Winstanley • August 13, 2020 Apart from the top printing, structurally from the outside they are identical, however the internal architecture is significantly different! Con la creación de Embalajes Ecológicos Transpack en 1993, fuimos pioneros en nuestra apuesta por el cartón, la sostenibilidad y la innovación. Nuestro equipo de profesionales expertos en embalaje es capaz de aportar valor para cada cliente, diseñando una propuesta de packaging y un servicio a medida. CONTACTAR CONÓCENOS Ventajas de tratar directamente con el fabricante de embalaje La confianza de trabajar con los mejores Mejora de la eficiencia El embalaje es uno de los aspectos donde más fácilmente se pueden identificar mejoras de la eficiencia de su empresa. Desde el embalaje industrial para uso interno o de la planta de producción, hasta el envase de cartón , Transpack Group puede ayudarle a mejorar sus procesos y su cadena de valor, a disminuir los daños por transporte y a optimizar y reducir los stocks de embalaje necesarios. Fabricación a medida Como fabricantes de embalaje de cartón, no nos limitamos a ofrecer embalajes prefabricados, sino que ideamos soluciones completas que se adapten perfectamente al producto a embalar. En Transpack Group creemos que un embalaje diseñado a medida por nuestro personal experto no sólo puede repercutir positivamente en su imagen de marca y la satisfacción de sus propios clientes, sino que además puede ser la alternativa más eficiente para resolver muchos tipos de incidencias. Embalaje sostenible Como fabricantes de embalaje de cartón y de cartones complejos laminados, desde Transpack Group nos ofrecemos para ser su apoyo en la transición hacia un embalaje más sostenible, fabricado con materias primas recicladas y reciclables basadas en el papel y cartón. Todo ello sin renunciar a la calidad, la eficiencia y a los acabados técnicos cuando éstos sean necesarios para asegurar la resistencia y la calidad del embalaje. CONTACTAR Embalaje de cartón de calidad certificada Contar con Transpack Group como proveedor de todo tipo de embalaje de cartón supone una garantía de fiabilidad y seriedad, ya que cuenta con certificaciones y sellos que demuestran su implicación en la calidad de los embalajes que fabrica y en la mejora continua, sin olvidar el respeto y protección del medio ambiente. Calidad ISO 9001 Contamos con un sistema de gestión de la calidad, apostando por la mejora continua en los procesos y la satisfacción del cliente. En Embalajes Ecológicos Transpack, Medio Ambiente Pack y Le Tube Carton-Nedelec está auditado por la empresa SGS. Sostenibilidad FSC® La mayoría de nuestros papeles son reciclados u originarios de bosques bien gestionados. Pregúntanos por nuestros productos certificados FSC®. Huella de Carbono Huella de carbono La empresa Medio Ambiente Pack es una empresa inscrita en el registro de huella de carbono del Ministerio, con el objetivo de calcular y reducir su huella de carbono. Seguridad Alimentaria BRCGS Nuestros envases alimentarios fabricados en Medio Ambiente Pack cumplen con exigentes estándares de calidad y seguridad. Calidad ISO 9001 Contamos con un sistema de gestión de la calidad, apostando por la mejora continua en los procesos y la satisfacción del cliente. En la empresa Tubopack este sistema es auditado anualmente por DNV Business Assurance. Seguimos mejorando e innovando para anticiparnos a las necesidades del mercado. Fabricantes de embalaje de cartón sostenible Transpack Group apuesta por la sostenibilidad desde que iniciara su andadura en 1993 con la creación de Embalajes Ecológicos Transpack. En su momento, nos convertimos en una empresa pionera en apostar por la ecología y la sostenibilidad, y desde entonces hemos profundizado nuestro compromiso con el entorno y con las personas. Embalaje comprometido con el planeta El papel es la materia prima renovable y sostenible que utilizamos como base para todos nuestros embalajes. Nuestros papeles son de origen reciclado o controlado, logrando el menor impacto ambiental. Cerramos el círculo Controlar y separar los residuos nos permite avanzar hacia la economía circular. Los restos de papel y cartón se gestionan para que se puedan convertir de nuevo en pasta de papel, dándole una nueva vida a este valioso recurso.​ El embalaje evita el deterioro de mercancías El correcto diseño del cartón para embalaje y envíos evita los daños a los artículos durante su transporte y almacenaje. Gracias a ello, garantizamos que nuestros clientes reducen sus incidencias logísticas, evitando reponer producto dañado. Embalaje de cartón diseñado para el reciclaje Como fabricantes de embalaje sostenible, tenemos un departamento de diseño que estudia cada caso para optimizar el uso de materiales, asegurar la máxima reciclabilidad en colaboración con Itene y lograr la mayor eficiencia en el uso de los recursos productivos.​ Reducción de la huella de carbono de nuestro embalaje Nuestros embalajes de cartón permiten un envío eficiente. Gracias a un esfuerzo constante para lograr la eficiencia en sistemas productivos y transporte, y a un uso de materias primas locales y recicladas, logramos reducir el impacto ambiental de nuestras operaciones. En 2021 comenzamos la medición de la huella de carbono de nuestra actividad. Comprometidos con las personas Nos esforzamos por establecer relaciones a largo plazo con nuestros clientes, proveedores y empleados, proporcionando apoyo para la consecución de sus objetivos y proyectos. text: ITE Fabriks AB – Problemlösaren inom Plåt, Formning och Verktyg Fortsätt till innehållet 0454-990 90 ite@itefabriks.se Våra policyer Hållbarhet Dokument Nyheter Toggle Navigation Hem Om oss Hur vi arbetar Vår produktion Kontakta oss ite-hem admin 2024-06-04T06:51:49+02:00 Mångårig erfarenhet inom Plåt, Formning och Verktyg. Se hur vi kan hjälpa dig Kontakta oss En mångsidig legotillverkare med egen verktygsverkstad ITE är en komplett leverantör med lång erfarenhet av enkla och komplexa plåtkomponenter med högt ställda krav på kvalitet, leveranssäkerhet och flexibilitet. Vi erbjuder en komplett process från utveckling av produkten fram till ett logistikupplägg som anpassats till kundens önskemål. Allt för att gynna kundens konkurrenskraft. Verktyg Vi arbetar med erfarenhet och noggrannhet inom verktygs- och underhållsavdelningen Produktion Från enkla plåtdetaljer till komplexa konstruktioner med fokus på kvalitet och hållbarhet Sammansättning Över 50 års erfarenhet av högkvalitativ produktion för fordonsindustrin, energisektorn och mer, med fokus på hållbarhet och precision. Logistik Vi har utvecklat en effektiv logistik och hållbar leverans med långa traditioner och erfaren personal för att möta våra kunders behov, i en proaktiv och responsiv arbetsmiljö. Våra värdeord Genom våra långa traditioner så har vi utvecklat en hållbarhet och värdegrund som genomsyrar vår företagsamhet Omtanke Engagemang, jämlikhet och respekt på arbetsplatsen Vi är engagerade, vilket innebär att alla vill och får vara med. Vi accepterar inte kränkande beteende, särbehandling eller diskriminering. Vi arbetar för jämlikhet och jämställdhet på arbetsplatsen. Vi är positiva, nyfikna och intresserade av att anta nya utmaningar. Vi bryr oss utöver våra direkta arbetsuppgifter och medarbetaren är vår nyckel till framgång. Säkerhet Förebyggande och systematiskt arbetsmiljöarbete för trygghet och hälsa Vi är måna om att förebygga alla former av ohälsa och olycksfall. Skada eller ohälsa orsakad av eller på arbetet ser vi som ett misslyckande. Vi skall kunna arbeta i en trygg och säker miljö med ett bra arbetsklimat.Arbetsmiljöarbetet ska bedrivas förebyggande och systematiskt. För att uppnå en god arbetsmiljö är vi lyhörda, hjälpsamma och öppna för förändringar där alla bemöts med tillit o respekt. Kvalite Professionalism och kvalitet för kundnöjdhet och framgång Vi är professionella, vilket innebär att vi i varje situation håller det vi lovat. Vår främsta framgångsfaktor med kvalitetsarbetet är nöjda kunder. Företagets namn ska vara förknippat med hög kvalitét vad gäller personal, produkter och tjänster. Vi är kompetenta, förbereder oss, och arbetar faktabaserat. Vi är proaktiva och ger besked. Miljö Kontinuerlig förbättring och hållbarhet genom effektiv resursanvändning Vi arbetar ständigt med att förbättra verksamhetsledningssystemet, vår miljöprestanda och förebygga föroreningar för att kunna nå en miljömässigt hållbar verksamhet. Vår största miljöpåverkan kommer från förbrukning av energi och råmaterial. Vi arbetar oavbrutet vidare med att minska verksamhetens energiförbrukning, effektivisera materialförbrukningen samt att minska förbrukningen av processoljor med fokus på lösningsmedel. Genom ett aktivt arbete via vår interna miljögrupp skapas medvetenhet och engagemang kring verksamhetens miljöarbete för alla våra medarbetare oavsett befattning. However, one invisible adversary known as partial discharge (PD) can quietly undermine this protection over time. In this article, we’ll explore what partial discharge is, how it occurs, its types, and why early detection is vital. What Is Partial Discharge and How Does It Work? Partial discharge refers to a localised electrical discharge that happens within a small section of an insulating material under high voltage stress. Unlike a complete dielectric breakdown, PD does not bridge the gap between conductors fully but instead causes tiny leakage currents in voids, cracks, or impurities inside solid, liquid, or gaseous insulation. These minuscule discharges generate current pulses that slowly erode the insulation's integrity. Over time, this degradation can lead to catastrophic failure if left unchecked. Since partial discharge is typically silent and invisible, it often goes unnoticed until significant damage has already occurred. Causes Behind Partial Discharge Several factors can trigger partial discharge in insulation systems. Material defects such as voids, micro-cracks, or inclusions create weak spots where electric stress concentrates. Surface contamination and moisture further lower the dielectric strength of the insulation, encouraging discharge activity. Additionally, incorrect installation procedures or mechanical damage can introduce imperfections that become discharge sites. Aging and long-term exposure to electrical stress gradually degrade insulating materials, making them more susceptible to PD. Understanding these causes is essential for designing more reliable insulation systems and maintenance protocols. Partial discharge manifests in different forms depending on where and how it occurs within the insulation. The most common types include: 1. Corona Discharge - This type occurs in gas around uneven electric fields, producing self-sustaining ionisation. Visible light and a faint hissing sound often accompany corona discharge. It is prevalent near sharp edges or points in high-voltage equipment. 2. Floating Discharge - Floating discharge arises from design flaws or poor electrical contact in components, creating a partial voltage drop between high- and low-voltage electrodes. This uneven distribution encourages localised discharges based on impedance differences. 3. Surface Discharge - Happening along the interface between gas and solid or liquid insulators, surface discharge can occur on insulator walls, bushings, or winding notches in high-voltage motors. It typically affects junction points between two different insulating media. 4. Air-gap Discharge - Air-gap or internal discharge takes place when holes, cracks, or contaminants inside the insulation form gaps where discharge can occur. This type is usually found inside materials or between electrodes where insulation consistency is compromised. Why Early Detection of Partial Discharge Matters Because partial discharge evolves silently without immediate failure, it poses a hidden risk in electrical systems. Detecting PD early allows for timely intervention before insulation deteriorates to the point of full breakdown. In conclusion, partial discharge is a subtle yet destructive phenomenon that gradually wears down the electrical insulation essential for system reliability. By understanding its mechanisms, causes, and types, engineers and technicians can better safeguard high-voltage equipment through vigilant monitoring and maintenance. Staying ahead of partial discharge means protecting both infrastructure and operational continuity from costly failures. Using advanced infrared thermal imaging technology , firefighters can see through smoke, identify hotspots, locate trapped individuals, and make faster, more informed decisions during critical incidents. From search and rescue operations to fire suppression, thermal imaging cameras for firefighters improve visibility, enhance safety, and help save lives. Why Firefighting Thermal Imaging Cameras Are Essential Visibility is one of the greatest challenges firefighters face when entering a burning structure. Thick smoke can rapidly obscure exits, hazards, and victims, making firefighting and rescue operations significantly more dangerous. A firefighting thermal imaging camera detects infrared radiation emitted by heat sources rather than relying on visible light. This allows firefighters to effectively see through smoke and darkness, providing a clearer understanding of the environment around them. By identifying temperature differences, thermal imaging cameras help emergency responders: Locate fire sources quickly Identify hidden hotspots Detect victims during search and rescue operations Monitor fire spread Improve navigation in smoke-filled environments Assess potential structural risks This enhanced visibility allows crews to operate more efficiently while reducing unnecessary exposure to danger. Seeing Through Smoke with Thermal Imaging Technology One of the most valuable capabilities of an infrared firefighting camera is its ability to penetrate smoke and reveal thermal patterns that would otherwise remain hidden. During a fire, dense smoke can limit visibility to just a few centimetres. Thermal imaging cameras overcome this challenge by displaying heat signatures in real time, allowing firefighters to see: Fire locations hidden behind smoke Heat accumulation within rooms Potential escape routes Trapped occupants requiring rescue Dangerous changes in fire conditions This capability significantly improves the effectiveness of both firefighting and life-saving operations. Detecting Hotspots and Hidden Fire Sources Even after visible flames have been extinguished, dangerous hotspots can remain concealed within walls, ceilings, floors, or roofing structures. Firefighter thermal cameras allow crews to identify residual heat quickly and accurately, helping prevent reignition and reducing the risk of secondary fires. Thermal imaging technology can assist firefighters in: Detecting hidden embers Identifying smouldering materials Locating concealed fires inside structures Monitoring temperature changes during overhaul operations Verifying that extinguishment efforts have been successful By pinpointing heat sources with precision, crews can focus resources where they are needed most. Real-Time Thermal Imaging for Faster Decision-Making When responding to a fire, conditions can change within seconds. Incident commanders and frontline firefighters must continuously assess risks and adapt their tactics. A thermal imaging camera for firefighters provides real-time temperature information that helps crews make informed decisions throughout an incident. Benefits include: Enhanced situational awareness Improved communication between team members Faster identification of dangerous conditions Better allocation of firefighting resources More effective search and rescue operations The ability to monitor changing conditions in real time helps improve response efficiency and operational effectiveness. Improving Firefighter Safety with Thermal Imaging Cameras Firefighting is one of the most hazardous professions in the world. Protecting personnel is a priority for every fire service, and thermal imaging technology plays a critical role in improving firefighter safety. Advanced firefighting thermal imaging cameras can help identify: Structural weaknesses caused by heat Hidden hotspots High-temperature danger zones Areas at risk of flashover Hazardous conditions during interior firefighting operations By providing a clear thermal view of the environment, these cameras enable firefighters to make safer operational decisions and reduce exposure to unnecessary risks. SATIR Firefighting Thermal Imaging Cameras The SATIR Firefighting Thermal Imaging Camera is designed to meet the demanding requirements of modern fire and rescue professionals. Built for operation in extreme environments, it provides reliable thermal imaging performance when visibility is limited and rapid decision-making is essential. Key features include: Advanced infrared detection technology High-quality thermal image processing Rugged construction for harsh firefighting environments Long battery life for extended operations Easy-to-use controls for rapid deployment Options for handheld and vehicle-mounted applications SATIR's firefighting thermal cameras support a wide range of operational needs, including search and rescue, hotspot detection, fire scene assessment, and emergency response. Choosing the Right Thermal Imaging Camera for Firefighting Selecting the right thermal imaging camera for firefighting depends on operational requirements, environmental conditions, and intended use. Important considerations include: Thermal sensitivity Image quality and resolution Durability and environmental protection Battery performance Ease of use Compliance with firefighting standards Mounting and deployment options Investing in high-quality thermal imaging equipment can improve response effectiveness while helping fire services maintain high safety standards. Conclusion Firefighting thermal imaging cameras have transformed the way firefighters respond to emergencies. By enabling crews to see through smoke, locate victims, identify hotspots, assess hazards, and monitor fire behaviour in real time, thermal imaging technology has become an indispensable component of modern firefighting operations. Whether used for search and rescue, fire suppression, hotspot detection, or post-fire investigation, infrared thermal imaging cameras for firefighters improve visibility, safety, and operational efficiency. Skyline Photo By: John Doe Schaltfläche Unternehmen Als innovatives Unternehmen in der Kunststoffbranche sind wir spezialisiert auf die Verarbeitung von Duroplasten und hochwertigen Thermoplasten im Spritzgussverfahren. Mit unserem Fokus auf höchste Qualitätsstandards und kundenzentrierte Beratung stehen die Bedürfnisse unserer Kunden stets im Mittelpunkt. Unsere Flexibilität ermöglicht uns die Bewältigung sowohl von Großserienproduktionen als auch von Kleinserien. Mit unserer langjährigen Erfahrung im Werkzeugbau lösen wir Abstimmungsprobleme und ermöglichen kurzfristig Werkzeugänderungen. Zusätzlich bieten wir Nachbehandlungsverfahren wie Heißprägung und Ultraschallschweißung sowie Montagearbeiten von Baugruppen an, um unseren Kunden ein umfassendes Leistungsspektrum in Österreich zu bieten. REFERENZEN Erfolgreich seit 1923 Die Firma Greminger, gegründet von Herrn Ing. Max Greminger im Jahr 1923, begann als Hersteller von Elektrogeräten in Wattens. Unter der Leitung von Ing. Kurt Greminger expandierte das Unternehmen in den fünfziger Jahren nach Kolsass mit dem Beginn der Kunststoffverarbeitung. Besonders stark war Greminger in der Verarbeitung von Verbundteilen aus Kunststoff und Metall, was für die Belieferung der Elektroindustrie von großer Bedeutung war. 1980 übernahm Dipl.-Ing. Kurt Greminger das Unternehmen in der dritten Generation. Neben den traditionellen Abnehmern aus verschiedenen Branchen erweiterte sich der Kundenstamm auf internationale Auftraggeber, wodurch die Exportquote bis zu 30 % des Umsatzes ausmachte. Nosotros te guiamos desde la primera consulta hasta el producto terminado. Más de 35 años de experiencia en el envasado de sachets para marcas cosméticas y de cuidado personal. Clientes en más de 20 países, ayudándoles a convertir sus productos en muestras, monodosis y promociones listas para el mercado. Conclusión: Más de 35 años de experiencia en más de 20 países respaldan nuestra trayectoria. impresión envasado Producción integrada: imprimimos y envasamos en una sola planta Realizamos todas las fases del proyecto: impresión y envasado. Al realizarlas en la misma planta, evitamos intermediarios, simplificamos la comunicación y acompañamos tu proyecto de forma más ágil y rápida. Nuestro departamento de Preimpresión adapta tus diseños para su impresión en flexografía. Conclusión: La unificación de procesos en la misma planta permite simplificar la gestión y avanzar con mayor agilidad. Desde 5.000 unidades No hay por qué empezar con grandes tiradas. Muchas marcas buscan validar un lanzamiento o realizar una primera producción ajustada antes de escalar. En Perfum Packaging trabajamos desde 5.000 unidades, ofreciendo una solución flexible para marcas que necesitan fabricar sachets con calidad profesional sin asumir volúmenes excesivos desde el inicio. ¿Quieres hacer muestras de productos cosméticos o de cuidado personal y no sabes por dónde empezar? Convertir una crema, un gel, un sérum o cualquier otro producto cosmético en un sachet implica tomar decisiones como formato, dosis, material o impresión. En Perfum Packaging te ayudamos a ordenar esas decisiones y convertirlas en un proceso sencillo. 5 preguntas clave para crear un sachet Antes de fabricar un sachet, conviene definir algunos aspectos técnicos y comerciales. ¿Cómo es mi producto? No se comporta igual una crema, un gel, un aceite, una mascarilla o un producto líquido. Para elegir bien el sachet hay que valorar la viscosidad, la presencia de ingredientes oleaginosos, el comportamiento durante el llenado, la estabilidad o la compatibilidad con el material. ¿Qué dosis es la adecuada? La dosis influye en el tamaño del sobre, el coste unitario, la experiencia de uso y la percepción del consumidor. Más cantidad no siempre significa una mejor muestra. Una dosis bien definida debe permitir probar el producto correctamente sin encarecer el proyecto ni sobredimensionar el envase. ¿Qué formato conviene? El formato depende del objetivo de la campaña y del tipo de producto. Puedes necesitar un sachet individual para una muestra o monodosis, un sachet twin para dos productos complementarios, o un sachet con toallita para productos líquidos impregnados. La elección del formato debe responder al uso final: sampling, venta monodosis, farmacia, e-commerce, perfumería o acción promocional. ¿Qué material es el más conveniente? En algunos casos será conveniente una estructura tradicional de alta barrera, incluso con aluminio. En otros, puede tener más sentido estudiar alternativas más orientadas a reciclabilidad, como estructuras más simples o monomateriales. Además, el material debe alinearse con la imagen que quieres proyectar. ¿El sachet debe ser reciclable? La elección del material no puede separarse del contexto regulatorio europeo. El PPWR, Reglamento Europeo de Envases y Residuos, impulsa envases diseñados para reciclaje, estructuras más simples, reducción de peso y volumen, y mayor responsabilidad sobre el final de vida del packaging. Por eso conviene valorar desde el inicio si el proyecto puede utilizar una estructura más simple, como un sachet monomaterial PP, o si la fórmula necesita una barrera superior. Un embalaje para cada promoción Podemos entregar tus sachets en el subembalaje que necesites: cajas, estuches de cartón, bolsas minigrip o el packaging que nos proporciones. Así recibes el producto preparado para sampling, e-commerce, farmacia, promociones o distribución. Conclusión: En Perfum Packaging te ayudamos a tomar las decisiones clave del proyecto y a convertirlas en un proceso sencillo. Diseñando tu sachet un formato y un material para cada proyecto. un formato para cada objetivo Sachet individual ideal para una sola aplicación. Sachet con toallita para productos líquidos impregnados en toallita de celulosa o viscosa biodegradable. Sachets twin para rutinas de dos pasos o productos complementarios. Un material para cada proyecto multimaterial con aluminio : para productos muy sensibles puede ser necesario utilizar estructuras multicapa de alta barrera con aluminio, que ayudan a conservar mejor el producto durante su vida útil. Complejo multicapa poliéster blanco PET / tinta blanca / Al / PE Complejo multicapa poliéster aluminio PET / Al / PE. Complejo multicapa papel estucado papel estucado / PE / Al / RT Complejo multicapa papel kraft natural papel kraft natural / PE / Al / Surlyn. Complejo multicapa papel kraft blanco papel kraft blanco / PE / Al / Surlyn. complejo multicapa monomaterial polipropileno blanco El PPWR está cambiando la forma de diseñar envases en Europa. Muchos sachets tradicionales son estructuras multicapa que combinan diferentes materiales para conseguir una alta barrera, y esa complejidad puede dificultar su reciclabilidad. El sachet monomaterial está basado en polipropileno y, al utilizar una familia de material más homogénea, reduce la complejidad. Puede ser adecuado para marcas que quieren anticiparse a un mercado donde la reciclabilidad será cada vez más importante. Complejo multicapa monomaterial polipropileno blanco: BOPP / Met BOPP / PPW. Conclusión: Te guiamos para elegir el material y el formato más adecuados según el objetivo de tu proyecto. proyectos realizados una selección de sachets fabricados en diferentes formatos, materiales y acabados. ❮ ❯ Normativa cosmética, calidad certificada y etiquetado Un sachet cosmético no solo debe ser atractivo y funcional. También debe respetar los requisitos aplicables al producto, al etiquetado y al mercado de destino. Perfum Packaging trabaja con un sistema de calidad y buenas prácticas respaldado por ISO 9001, ISO 22716, certificado BPF de productos cosméticos expedido por la AEMPS e ISO 14001. Estas certificaciones refuerzan la forma de trabajar: control, trazabilidad, higiene, documentación, mejora continua y responsabilidad ambiental. Conocemos las exigencias del entorno cosmético y te asesoramos para cumplir con la legislación europea vigente sobre sachets cosméticos. Validamos lo importante antes de fabricar Cuando el proyecto lo requiere, podemos ayudarte a comprobar que el sachet funciona correctamente con tu producto. Se pueden realizar prueba de impresión, prueba de envasado y test de compatibilidad. Una prueba bien planteada evita problemas posteriores. Conclusión: Nuestro sistema de trabajo está respaldado por ISO 9001, ISO 22716, BPF AEMPS e ISO 14001. FAQs Aquí resolvemos dudas habituales sobre cantidades, materiales, certificaciones, pruebas previas y la información necesaria para orientar cada proyecto. ¿Puedo pedir presupuesto si no sé exactamente qué sachet necesito? Sí. Es habitual que el cliente no tenga definido el formato, la dosis o el material. Con información básica sobre tu producto podemos orientarte sobre la solución más adecuada. ¿Desde qué cantidad puedo fabricar sachets? Desde 5.000 unidades. ¿Perfum Packaging imprime y envasa? Sí. Realizamos todas las fases del proyecto: impresión y envasado, evitando intermediarios y agilizando el proyecto. ¿Qué tipo de productos se pueden envasar en sachet? Productos cosméticos y de cuidado personal como cremas, geles, aceites, mascarillas, líquidos, sérums, champús, lociones, productos con toallita y otros productos similares. ¿Cómo sé qué material necesita mi producto? El material se elige según la fórmula, la barrera necesaria, la imagen de marca, la impresión, la reciclabilidad y el canal de distribución. Algunos productos sensibles pueden requerir estructuras con aluminio; otros pueden valorarse en estructuras más orientadas a reciclabilidad. ¿Qué es el sachet monomaterial PP? Es una estructura basada en polipropileno que utiliza una familia de material más homogénea, reduciendo la complejidad frente a muchos laminados multimaterial. Puede ser interesante para proyectos orientados a diseño para reciclaje, siempre que sea compatible con la fórmula y la barrera necesaria. ¿El monomaterial PP cumple automáticamente el PPWR? No conviene afirmarlo así. El monomaterial PP está alineado con criterios de diseño para reciclabilidad, pero el cumplimiento dependerá de los requisitos aplicables, la clasificación final del envase y los desarrollos técnicos del reglamento previstos para 2028. ¿Qué certificaciones tiene Perfum Packaging? Perfum Packaging trabaja con un sistema respaldado por ISO 9001, ISO 22716, certificado BPF de productos cosméticos expedido por la AEMPS e ISO 14001. Estas certificaciones refuerzan control, trazabilidad, higiene, documentación, mejora continua y responsabilidad ambiental. ¿Se pueden hacer pruebas antes de producir? Sí, cuando el proyecto lo requiere. Se pueden realizar pruebas de impresión, de envasado y test de compatibilidad para comprobar que el sachet funciona correctamente con el producto. Conclusión: Aquí resolvemos dudas habituales sobre cantidades, materiales, certificaciones, pruebas previas y la información necesaria para orientar cada proyecto. También, en Ballester ofrecen servicio de inyección de plásticos a terceros. En Matricería y Plásticos Ballester se caracterizan por conocer exactamente lo que el público objetivo requiere: buen servicio, calidad, rápidos tiempos de respuesta y ejecución y costes competitivos. En la organización cuentan con tecnología de punta, control de calidad y la supervisión adecuada. Una de las principales ventajas de Matricería y Plásticos Ballester es la amplia cantidad de productos estándar en stock y una logística efectiva y eficaz en todos y cada uno de sus procesos. Entre los productos más destacados son los tapones para botellas PET y de polietileno. Ofrecen tapas para las bocas estándar: 20/410, 24/415, 28/410 y 25/30. text: Cash-Flow Analytics & AI Credit Scoring for Banks | Prestatech Prestatech has been recognized among the World’s Top FinTech Companies 2026 by CNBC Products Solutions Company Log in We read the heartbeat of your borrowers Bank account data analytics and document automation tools to grow your book with the same risk appetite. Legacy workflows are too slow, too expensive, and too error-prone to keep up — and the cost of getting it wrong compounds fast. 40% of SME loan applicants abandon the process if a decision takes longer than 48 hours. 5–10x the operational cost per loan when credit analysis relies on manual document review and spreadsheet-based cash flow calculations. 15–25% of portfolio losses are linked to incomplete financial visibility at the point of origination. Prestatech eliminates these bottlenecks Approve faster. Automated document capture, transaction enrichment, and cashflow scoring compress weeks of analysis into minutes. Approve more. Deeper financial visibility means you can confidently say yes to applicants that traditional credit checks would reject. Approve smarter. Predictive KPIs and real-time behavioural signals replace gut feel with data-driven precision — at origination and throughout the loan lifecycle. Book demo Among our Clients Our Partners With Prestatech you can enhance your lending and monitoring proposition Approve 10-35% more customers without increasing risk exposure Cut portfolio losses by 15-40% with predictive risk insights Accelerate loan decisions by 5x with automated data processing Reduce manual review time by 80% through intelligent document automation Book demo FAQs What is Prestatech and who uses it? Prestatech is an intelligent lending-automation platform that blends machine-learning document processing with real-time cash-flow analytics to speed credit decisions for SME and consumer lenders. How does your Cash-Flow Scoring work? We analyse a borrower’s complete bank-account transaction history, transform thousands of signals into a 0-100 synthetic score, and surface risk factors impossible to see in traditional bureau data. What data sources can the platform read? Our APIs ingest open-banking feeds, uploaded financial statements, invoices, payslips and other documents, standardising them into one analytics model. What types of data do you analyze? Bank-account transactions plus alternative financial data (for both consumers and SMEs) feed our analytics and scoring models. How does Intelligent Document Automation reduce manual credit work? Our computer-vision system automatically captures and analyzes any document type, speeding credit assessment, onboarding, and back-office tasks. Are you compliant with data-security standards like GDPR and ISO 27001? Yes—our secure cloud infrastructure follows enterprise-grade standards, including ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance. What measurable outcomes can lenders expect? Clients see faster approvals and lower default rates by using real-time analytics and data-driven insights throughout the credit lifecycle. Who is Prestatech built for? For any type of Bank and Modern lenders focused on SME and consumer credit who want to automate risk intelligence and decisioning. How do real-time bank-account analytics improve credit decisions? Streaming transaction insights reveal cash-flow health and behavioral patterns instantly, enabling more accurate, timely lending decisions. Why do leading banks choose Prestatech for cash‑flow scoring? Major European banks use our cash‑flow analytics. A Tier‑1 bank case showed ECB‑approved cash‑flow models, >80% acceptance for statement parsing, ~70% time saved per dossier, and our reports helped resolve 32% of UTP cases. What ROI or efficiency gains can we expect with cash flow analytics? Customers see a 20% increase in approvals for borrowers without a traditional credit history, three-month early distress detection, an 80% reduction in manual tasks, and five-times faster loan response. At portfolio scale, they also achieve a 25 to 40% improvement in credit decision accuracy and an 80% reduction in manual portfolio review time. Is Prestatech recognized globally by independent rankings? Yes. Prestatech announced its inclusion in CNBC & Statista’s World’s Top FinTech Companies 2025 ranking as a leader in cash-flow analytics category. Why is cash‑flow analysis essential in modern underwriting? Supervisors now stress robust, prospective cash‑flow assessment in loan origination, and research shows transaction‑level data improves risk prediction and expands access for thin‑file borrowers. Cash‑flow underwriting adds predictive power beyond bureau data and supports stronger monitoring. How does Prestatech use AI in its solutions ? Unlike black-box scoring, our computer vision and analytics engines are deterministic, replicable, and fully traceable, producing explainable outputs at every step. Every output can be audited and defended, with full traceability for regulators and internal audit, which is critical for model risk governance in regulated lending and lets risk teams stand behind every decision. How quickly can Prestatechs software be implemented for my bank? Our architecture is API-first, so we slot into existing workflows and core systems without rip-and-replace. Pre-built widgets go live in days, full API integration typically takes one to two weeks, and enterprise data-lake deployments run eight to twelve weeks. How customizable are the Prestatech products for different lending institutions and loan products? All parameters are configured to each lender's policies, including pass/fail thresholds, referral rules, risk appetite, and tag taxonomy. We support everything from consumer, sub-prime SME to corporate, and our team advises on calibration based on portfolio mix and risk profile. Can Prestatech’s solutions improve client retention? Yes. Real-time financial health monitoring surfaces early signals such as cashflow deterioration, churn risk, and cross-sell opportunities, so bankers can intervene with the right offer at the right time. Automating manual document and underwriting work also frees relationship managers to spend more time with customers and anticipate needs rather than react to them. What types of loans can Prestatech’s solutions handle? Our solutions handle SMB and consumer lending across term loans, cash advances, credit cards, mortgages, equipment finance, and specialty credit. The analytics layer supports both origination (affordability and financial health scoring) and portfolio monitoring (early warning and repayment capacity). Which systems does Prestatech integrate with? Our platform is system-agnostic and API-first. We connect to core banking platforms, LOS, and proprietary systems, as well as major data lakes such as AWS, Azure, GCP, and Snowflake. Integration channels include REST APIs, pre-built widgets, SFTP for bulk ingestion, and dashboards for brokers and underwriters. Consumer & SME Annuity · linear · bullet repayment Multi-currency Built-in collections & recovery On this page The full lifecycle in one platform Repayment structures that match your product Mid-loan flexibility Decisioning and compliance Collections and recovery The full lifecycle in one platform Instalment lending has a long operational tail. Between origination and final repayment, a loan touches underwriting, repayment scheduling, holiday requests, early settlement, missed payments, collections, and closure. Most platforms handle the front end well. The back end is where operational cost accumulates. CreditOnline manages the complete instalment lifecycle - from application and credit decision through servicing, mid-loan amendments, and recovery - without handoffs to separate systems. Repayment structures that match your product Not every instalment product follows the same schedule. Three repayment methods are supported natively: Annuity - equal periodic payments where the proportion of interest vs. principal shifts over time. Standard for most consumer instalment products. Linear - fixed principal payments with decreasing interest, resulting in higher early payments and lower later ones. Common in SME and asset-backed lending. Bullet - interest-only payments throughout the term with full principal at maturity. Used in bridging finance and certain business loan structures. All three are configurable at origination. Your team sets the parameters; the platform handles the arithmetic. Mid-loan flexibility Borrower circumstances change. The platform handles mid-loan amendments without manual recalculation: Payment holidays - partial or full, applied to any payment in the schedule, with automatic interest recalculation for the remaining term. Early repayment - borrowers settle ahead of schedule; the system recalculates the outstanding balance, applies any early settlement fee, and closes the account cleanly. Payment date changes - schedule shifts for payday alignment or other circumstances, with downstream recalculation applied automatically. Decisioning and compliance CreditOnline’s solvency assessment engine runs configurable scoring algorithms against applicant data alongside integrated bureau checks. The system connects to partner KYC and credit scoring services for live checks at origination. For EU lenders, the platform supports the documentation requirements under the Consumer Credit Directive - automated document generation covers loan agreements, repayment schedules, and pre-contractual disclosures. Collections and recovery Late payments are a normal part of instalment lending. The platform handles them without leaving the system: Automated late fee calculation and application on missed payments Configurable reminder sequences - SMS, email, in-app - before and after due dates Recovery and trial process management for accounts in arrears Escalation paths configurable to your collections policy FAQ Common questions 01 Can we run multiple repayment schedule types on the same platform? Yes - annuity, linear, and bullet are all native, and mixable across products. 02 How does early repayment work? The system calculates the settlement figure automatically and closes the loan on payment. 03 Can we set our own late fee rules? Yes - fee type, grace period, and frequency are all configurable. 04 Does the platform handle multi-currency instalment products? Yes, with currency-specific fee configurations on the same platform instance. 05 What credit bureau integrations are available? Depends on your operating markets. Contact us for specifics. Building financial applications traditionally means months of development for basic features like payment processing, KYC compliance, and risk management. timveroOS changes this by providing production-ready financial components that you customize through code, not configuration. 1.1. The Problem 6-12 months to build basic lending platform from scratch Complex integrations with payment gateways, KYC providers, credit bureaus Regulatory compliance requirements that slow development Scalability challenges as your business grows 1.2. The timveroOS Solution 2-4 weeks to customize and deploy with pre-built components Built-in integrations for payments, documents, notifications Compliance frameworks for KYC, AML, reporting built-in Enterprise-scale architecture from day one 1.3. How It Works Basic (foundation) → Origination (new loans) → Servicing (active loans) Example: Personal loan process Customer applies → forms, documents (Basic + Origination) Loan approved → credit check, terms (Origination) Loan created → account setup (Origination → Servicing) Customer pays → balance updates (Servicing + Basic) 3.5. Key Platform Features The platform provides several key features that make building lending applications easier: 1. Consistent Patterns Everything follows the same pattern, so once you learn one part, you understand the whole platform: Entities - Store your business data (customers, loans, payments) Forms - Collect information from users with built-in validation Controllers - Handle user actions like creating or editing records Templates - Display information to users in web pages Example: Whether you’re working with customers, loan applications, or payments, they all follow the same pattern. 2. Automatic Business Rules The platform can automatically handle business logic for you: When a loan application is approved → automatically create the loan account When a payment is received → automatically update the loan balance When a payment is late → automatically calculate late fees When a loan is paid off → automatically close the account Example: You define the rule "charge a $25 late fee if payment is 10 days late" and the platform handles it automatically. 3. Complete Audit Trail Everything is tracked automatically for compliance and troubleshooting: Who made each change and when What the data looked like before and after changes Why each change happened (payment received, fee charged, etc.) Complete history of every loan account Example: You can see that on March 15th, John Smith made a $500 payment, which reduced his loan balance from $5,000 to $4,500. 3.6. Getting Started This section provides a quick introduction to building applications with the Timvero SDK. Follow this guide to get up and running in minutes and understand the core concepts through practical examples. 4.1. Prerequisites Before you begin, ensure you have the following installed: Java 21 or later - The platform requires modern Java features Maven 3.8+ - For dependency management and building PostgreSQL 16+ - Primary database for the platform IDE with Spring Boot support - IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, or VS Code 4.2. Quick Setup (5 minutes) Step 1: Clone and Configure Clone the example project : git clone https://github.com/timveroOS/timvero-example.git cd timvero-example Configure database connection in src/main/resources/application.properties : spring.datasource.url = jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/your_database spring.datasource.username = your_username spring.datasource.password = your_password Run the application : mvn spring-boot:run Access the application : Admin UI: http://localhost:8081 Portal API: http://localhost:8082 Step 2: Verify Installation Once running, you should see: Database tables automatically created via Flyway migrations Admin interface with navigation menu Sample data (if configured) No compilation errors in the console Troubleshooting Setup Issues Application Won’t Start Problem : Application failed to start with database connection errors Solution : Check database is running : # PostgreSQL status check sudo systemctl status postgresql # Or for Docker docker ps | grep postgres Verify database connection : # Test connection manually psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U your_username -d your_database Check application.properties : # Ensure these match your database setup spring.datasource.url = jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/your_database spring.datasource.username = your_username spring.datasource.password = your_password Common database URL mistakes : Wrong port (default PostgreSQL is 5432) Database name doesn’t exist User lacks permissions Flyway Migration Errors Problem : FlywayException: Migration checksum mismatch or migration failures Solution : Check migration file integrity : -- View migration history SELECT * FROM flyway_schema_history ORDER BY installed_rank DESC ; Reset migrations (development only) : # WARNING: This deletes all data mvn flyway:clean flyway:migrate Skip problematic migration (careful!) : # Only if you understand the implications mvn flyway:repair Port Already in Use Problem : Port 8081 was already in use or similar port conflicts Solution : Find what’s using the port : # Linux/Mac lsof -i :8081 # Windows netstat -ano | findstr :8081 Change application ports : # In application.properties server.port = 8090 management.server.port = 8091 Kill conflicting process : # Linux/Mac (replace PID with actual process ID) kill -9 PID # Windows taskkill /PID PID /F Java Version Issues Problem : UnsupportedClassVersionError or compilation failures Solution : Check Java version : java -version javac -version echo $JAVA_HOME Ensure Java 21+ : # Install Java 21 if needed # Ubuntu/Debian sudo apt install openjdk-21-jdk # macOS with Homebrew brew install openjdk@21 Set JAVA_HOME : # Linux/Mac - add to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc export JAVA_HOME = /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk # Windows - set in System Properties Maven Build Failures Problem : Maven dependency resolution or compilation errors Solution : Clean and rebuild : mvn clean compile mvn clean install -U # Force update dependencies Check Maven version : mvn --version # Should be 3.8+ Clear local repository : # Nuclear option - deletes all cached dependencies rm -rf ~/.m2/repository mvn clean install Can’t Access Admin UI Problem : Browser shows "This site can’t be reached" or connection refused Solution : Verify application started successfully : # Check logs for "Started Application in X seconds" tail -f logs/application.log Check correct URL : # Default URLs Admin UI: http://localhost:8081 Portal API: http://localhost:8082 # NOT http://localhost:8080 (that's often Spring Boot default) Check firewall/network : # Test port connectivity telnet localhost 8081 # Or curl -I http://localhost:8081 Database Tables Not Created Problem : Application starts but database is empty Solution : Verify migration files exist : ls -la src/main/resources/db/migration/ # Should see V*.sql files Check database permissions : -- User needs privileges to execute migration ALTER DATABASE your_database OWNER TO your_username ; 4.3. Your First Entity: Client Management (15 minutes) Let’s explore how the Client entity demonstrates the platform’s core patterns. The Client entity is already implemented in the example project, so you can see a complete working example. Entity Definition The Client entity demonstrates the platform’s entity structure: @Entity @Table @Audited @Indexed public class Client extends AbstractAuditable < UUID > implements NamedEntity , HasDocuments { @Embedded @Valid private IndividualInfo individualInfo ; @Embedded @Valid private ContactInfo contactInfo ; // getters and setters... } Key features: Extends AbstractAuditable : Automatic creation/modification tracking Implements NamedEntity : Provides display name functionality Composite structure : Contains IndividualInfo and ContactInfo components Search integration : @Indexed enables full-text search Audit support : @Audited tracks all changes Form Structure The ClientForm handles user input with validation: public class ClientForm { @Valid @NotNull private IndividualInfoForm individualInfo ; @Valid @NotNull private ContactInfoForm contactInfo ; // getters and setters... } Benefits: Nested validation : @Valid cascades validation to nested objects Clean separation : Form objects separate from entities Type safety : Strongly typed form fields Controller Implementation The main controller handles entity management: @Controller public class ClientController extends EntityController < UUID , Client , ClientForm > { // Inherits all CRUD functionality automatically } Actions provide specific operations (buttons in the UI): @Controller public class CreateClientAction extends EntityCreateController < UUID , Client , ClientForm > { @Override protected boolean isOwnPage () { return false ; } } @Controller public class EditClientAction extends EditEntityActionController < UUID , Client , ClientForm > { // Handles the edit button functionality } What you get automatically {ok} Create, Read, Update, Delete operations {ok} Form validation and error handling {ok} List view with search and filtering {ok} Responsive web interface {ok} Audit logging of all changes Form Service Layer The service layer handles business logic and data mapping: @Service public class ClientFormService extends EntityFormService < Client , ClientForm , UUID > { // Inherits entity-form mapping and persistence operations } The service requires a corresponding MapStruct mapper for entity-form conversion: @Mapper public interface ClientFormMapper extends EntityToFormMapper < Client , ClientForm > { // MapStruct automatically generates implementation for bidirectional mapping } Template Integration The HTML template demonstrates the form component system: <th:block th:insert= "~{/form/components :: text( #{client.individualInfo.fullName}, 'individualInfo.fullName', 'v-required v-name')}" /> <th:block th:insert= "~{/form/components :: text( #{client.contactInfo.email}, 'contactInfo.email', 'v-required v-email')}" /> 4.4. Essential Concepts (10 minutes) Entity-Form-Controller Pattern The platform follows a consistent architectural pattern: Table 1. Platform Architecture Pattern Component Purpose Example Entity JPA entity with business logic and relationships Client - stores customer data with audit trail Form DTO for user input with validation rules ClientForm - handles form submission and validation Controller Main entity controller providing CRUD operations ClientController - handles entity management Actions Specific operation buttons in the UI CreateClientAction , EditClientAction - handle specific operations Service Business logic and entity-form mapping ClientFormService - converts between entities and forms Mapper Automatic bidirectional object mapping ClientFormMapper - MapStruct-generated conversions Automatic Features Once you create the basic structure following this pattern, the platform automatically provides: CRUD Operations : Complete create, read, update, delete functionality Form Validation : Client-side and server-side validation Database Migrations : Automatic schema generation and versioning Search and Filtering : Full-text search and advanced filtering Audit Logging : Complete change history tracking Responsive UI : Mobile-friendly web interface Security Integration : Authentication and authorization API Endpoints : RESTful API for external integration Data Flow Understanding the data flow helps you work effectively with the platform: User Input → Form Validation → Controller → Service → Mapper → Entity → Database ↓ Template Rendering ← Form Object ← Mapper ← Entity ← Database Query Troubleshooting Entity-Form-Controller Issues Form Validation Not Working Problem : Form submits with invalid data or validation messages don’t appear Solution : Check validation annotations : // Ensure @Valid is present on nested objects @Valid @NotNull private IndividualInfoForm individualInfo ; Verify form component validation classes : <!-- Ensure validation CSS classes are included --> <th:block th:insert= "~{/form/components :: text( #{client.individualInfo.fullName}, 'individualInfo.fullName', 'v-required v-name')}" /> Controller Actions Not Appearing Problem : Create/Edit buttons don’t show up in the UI Solution : Check controller annotations : @Controller // Must be @Controller, not @RestController public class CreateClientAction extends EntityCreateController < UUID , Client , ClientForm > { } Check template includes actions : <!-- Ensure action templates are included --> <div th:replace= "~{/entity/actions :: entityActions}" ></div> Form Fields Not Displaying Problem : Form renders but specific fields are missing or empty Solution : Check form component syntax : <!-- Ensure proper Thymeleaf fragment syntax --> <th:block th:insert= "~{/form/components :: text( #{client.individualInfo.fullName}, 'individualInfo.fullName', 'v-required v-name')}" /> Verify i18n message keys exist : # In messages.properties client.individualInfo.fullName = Full Name 4.5. Common Scenarios (20 minutes) Adding Custom Validation Enhance the Client form with custom business rules: public class ClientForm { @NotBlank @Size ( min = 2 , max = 100 , message = "Name must be between 2 and 100 characters" ) private String fullName ; @NotBlank @Email ( message = "Please provide a valid email address" ) private String email ; @NotBlank @Phone ( message = "Please provide a valid phone number" ) private String phone ; @PastOrPresent ( message = "Birth date cannot be in the future" ) private LocalDate dateOfBirth ; } Implementing Business Logic with Entity Checkers Create automated workflows that respond to client changes: @Component public class ClientWelcomeChecker extends EntityChecker < Client > { @Override protected void registerListeners ( CheckerListenerRegistry < Client > registry ) { // Trigger when a new client is created registry . entityChange (). inserted (); } @Override protected boolean isAvailable ( Client client ) { // Only for clients with complete contact information return client . getContactInfo () != null && client . getContactInfo (). getEmail () != null ; } @Override protected void perform ( Client client ) { // Send welcome email to new clients emailService . sendWelcomeEmail ( client ); log . info ( "Welcome email sent to client: {}" , client . getIndividualInfo (). getFullName ()); } } Adding Document Management Enable clients to upload required documents: // 1. Make Client support documents @Entity public class Client extends AbstractAuditable < UUID > implements HasDocuments { // Existing client implementation } // 2. Configure document types @Configuration public class ClientDocumentConfiguration { public static final EntityDocumentType ID_DOCUMENT = new EntityDocumentType ( "ID_DOCUMENT" ); public static final EntityDocumentType PROOF_OF_ADDRESS = new EntityDocumentType ( "PROOF_OF_ADDRESS" ); @Bean DocumentTypeAssociation < Client > clientRequiredDocuments () { return DocumentTypeAssociation . forEntityClass ( Client . class ) . required ( ID_DOCUMENT ) . required ( PROOF_OF_ADDRESS ) . build (); } } // 3. Add document management tab @Controller @Order ( 1000 ) public class ClientDocumentsTab extends EntityDocumentTabController < Client > { @Override public boolean isVisible ( Client client ) { return true ; // Always show documents tab for clients } } Integrating External Data Sources Fetch additional data from external APIs: // 1. Create a data source subject interface public interface CreditCheckSubject { String getNationalId (); String getFullName (); } // 2. Implement the interface in your entity @Entity public class Client implements CreditCheckSubject { @Override public String getNationalId () { return getIndividualInfo (). getNationalId (); } @Override public String getFullName () { return getIndividualInfo (). getFullName (); } } // 3. Create the data source implementation @Service ( "creditCheck" ) public class CreditCheckDataSource implements MappedDataSource < CreditCheckSubject , CreditReport > { @Override public Class < CreditReport > getType () { return CreditReport . class ; } @Override public Content getData ( CreditCheckSubject subject ) throws Exception { // Call external credit check API String response = creditCheckApi . checkCredit ( subject . getNationalId (), subject . getFullName () ); return new Content ( response . getBytes (), MediaType . APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE ); } @Override public CreditReport parseRecord ( Content data ) throws Exception { return objectMapper . readValue ( data . getData (), CreditReport . class ); } } 4.6.
