Application Setup timveroOS uses a hierarchical Spring context: a non-web parent and multiple child web applications. Each child runs on its own port with its own configuration. 5.1. Entry Point public class ExampleApplication { public static void main ( String [] args ) { // Parent context — not a web application. // BaseConfiguration is provided by the core. // CustomConfiguration is your project-specific configuration. SpringApplicationBuilder parentBuilder = new SpringApplicationBuilder ( BaseConfiguration . class , CustomConfiguration . class ) . web ( WebApplicationType . NONE ); ConfigurableApplicationContext parentContext = parentBuilder . run ( args ); try { // Main admin interface parentBuilder . child ( WebMvcConfig . class , CustomWebConfiguration . class ) . properties ( "spring.config.name=main" ) . run ( args ); // REST API (optional) parentBuilder . child ( PortalWebConfiguration . class ) . properties ( "spring.config.name=portal" ) . run ( args ); // Workflow engine (optional) parentBuilder . child ( ExternalProcessWebMvcConfig . class ) . properties ( "spring.config.name=workflow" ) . run ( args ); } catch ( Throwable e ) { parentContext . close (); throw e ; } } } Each child context loads its own properties file via spring.config.name (e.g. main.properties , portal.properties , workflow.properties ). Use this to configure ports, context paths, and other settings per child. 5.2. Spring Boot Actuator Actuator provides health checks, metrics, and monitoring endpoints. It is not included by default — add it explicitly if needed: <dependency> <groupId> org.springframework.boot </groupId> <artifactId> spring-boot-starter-actuator </artifactId> </dependency> Management Port Each child context should configure its own Actuator port. Use -1 to disable Actuator for a child, or a dedicated port to expose it: # Expose Actuator on a dedicated port (main.properties) management.server.port = 8189 This keeps management endpoints separate from application traffic. Endpoint Exposure By default, only health is exposed over HTTP. Control which endpoints are available: # Disable all web endpoints management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclude = * # Or selectively enable specific endpoints management.endpoints.web.exposure.include = health,info,metrics # Disable a specific endpoint entirely management.endpoint.health.enabled = false # Show full health details (default: "never") management.endpoint.health.show-details = always Kubernetes Probes Enable liveness and readiness probes for Kubernetes deployments: # Enable /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled = true # Customize liveness probe indicators management.endpoint.health.group.liveness.include = livenessState,webContexts For the full list of Actuator properties and endpoints, see the Spring Boot Actuator documentation . 6. Password Management timveroOS provides built-in password security for the back-office user authentication system. Configure account lockout, password expiration, and password validation rules through the password.* properties in your application.properties file. 6.1. Account Lockout The platform locks a user account after too many consecutive failed login attempts within a rolling time window. With the defaults below, 3 failures inside any 30-minute window triggers a lockout. The lock is automatically lifted once the oldest recorded attempt falls outside the window. # Maximum number of failed attempts within the window before the account is locked password.attempts = 3 # Number of minutes a failed attempt remains counted toward the lockout threshold password.block.minutes = 30 Failed-attempt counters are held in memory and are reset if the application restarts. Increase password.attempts or decrease password.block.minutes to reduce friction for legitimate users. For stricter security, do the opposite. When the number of remaining attempts drops to 3 or fewer, the login form shows the exact count. An administrator can unlock an account at any time, which clears all recorded failed attempts immediately. 6.2. Password Expiration Passwords expire after a configurable number of days, counted from the moment the password was last set. Once expired, the user is prompted to change their password on the next login. # Number of days before a password expires and must be changed password.lifetime.days = 90 A password flagged as single-use (e.g. a temporary reset password) is treated as expired immediately, regardless of this setting. 6.3. Password Change Flow When a user’s password has expired, the login page displays a change-password form. The new password must differ from the current one and satisfy the password.pattern regex. After a successful change the user is redirected to the login page to authenticate with the new password. 6.4. Temporary Passwords A 12-character random password is generated when a new user is created or when an administrator resets a user’s password. It is marked as single-use, so the user must change it on their very first login (see Password Expiration ). A notification containing the temporary password is sent automatically. 6.5. Configuration Reference Property Default Description password.attempts 3 Maximum number of failed login attempts allowed within the window before the account is locked. password.block.minutes 30 Length of the rolling window (in minutes) used to count failed login attempts. password.lifetime.days 90 Number of days after which a password expires and must be changed. password.pattern .* Java regex pattern that a new password must match. Use .* to allow any value (no restriction). 7. Data model setup This section describes how to set up and manage the data model using SQL file autogeneration and Flyway migrations. 7.1. SQL File Autogeneration The platform automatically generates SQL files based on your entity definitions. This process creates the necessary database schema files that can be used with Flyway for database migrations. Automatic Generation Process After the class is configured, run the application. The system will analyze changes in the data model of Java classes and generate an SQL script with the necessary changes V241012192920.sql in the project’s home directory ( application.home= path ), in the subdirectory hbm2ddl . The generation process works as follows: Entity Analysis : The system scans all JPA entity classes for changes Schema Comparison : Compares current entity definitions with the existing database schema SQL Generation : Creates appropriate DDL statements (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) for detected changes File Creation : Generates timestamped migration files in the hbm2ddl directory Migration Integration : Files can be moved to Flyway migration directory for deployment Entity Definition Example Let’s look at the Participant entity as an example: @Entity @Table @Audited public class Participant extends AbstractAuditable implements NamedEntity , GithubDataSourceSubject , HasDocuments , ProcessEntity , DocusignSigner , HasPendingDecisions , HasMetric { public static final String DECISION_OWNER_TYPE = "PARTICIPANT" ; @Column ( nullable = false ) @Enumerated ( value = EnumType . STRING ) private ParticipantStatus status = ParticipantStatus . NEW ; @ElementCollection ( fetch = FetchType . EAGER ) @Enumerated ( EnumType . STRING ) private Set < ParticipantRole > roles ; @ManyToOne ( fetch = EAGER ) @JoinColumn ( nullable = false , updatable = false ) private Application application ; @ManyToOne ( fetch = EAGER ) @JoinColumn ( nullable = false , updatable = false ) private Client client ; @Column ( nullable = false ) @Enumerated ( STRING ) private Employment employment ; @Column ( nullable = false ) @Enumerated ( STRING ) private Periodicity howOftenIncomeIsPaid ; @Embedded private MonetaryAmount totalAnnualIncome ; @Embedded private MonetaryAmount monthlyOutgoings ; @Column private String githubUsername ; // getters and setters... } Enum Definitions The entity uses several enums that define the possible values: ParticipantStatus enum public enum ParticipantStatus implements InEnum < ParticipantStatus > { NEW , IN_PROCESS , MANUAL_APPROVAL , APPROVED , DECLINED , VOID ; public boolean isActive () { return ! this . in ( DECLINED , VOID ); } } Employment enum public enum Employment { EMPLOYED , HOMEMAKER , UNEMPLOYED , RETIRED , SELF_EMPLOYED } Periodicity enum public enum Periodicity { MONTHLY , FORTNIGHTLY , WEEKLY , UNDEFINED } 7.2. Flyway Migration Integration Migration File Structure Flyway migration files are stored in the src/main/resources/db/migration/ directory and follow the naming convention: V{version}__{description}.sql For example: V250530170222__init.sql V250609220043__participantStatus.sql Generated SQL Example Based on the Participant entity definition, the system generates the following SQL: create table participant ( id uuid not null , created_at timestamp ( 6 ) with time zone not null , updated_at timestamp ( 6 ) with time zone not null , employment varchar ( 255 ) not null , how_often_income_is_paid varchar ( 255 ) not null , monthly_outgoings_currency varchar ( 3 ), monthly_outgoings_number numeric ( 19 , 2 ), total_annual_income_currency varchar ( 3 ), total_annual_income_number numeric ( 19 , 2 ), created_by uuid , updated_by uuid , -- Foreign key to application table application_id uuid not null , -- Foreign key to client table client_id uuid not null , primary key ( id ) ); -- Foreign key constraints for participant table -- Links participant to their associated loan application alter table if exists participant add constraint FKa8akyngsbkcpy4ev19q53x56h foreign key ( application_id ) references application ; -- Links participant to their client profile containing personal information alter table if exists participant add constraint FKcmejtugfqk653qthh0jalsx54 foreign key ( client_id ) references client ; Migration Workflow Entity Definition : Define your entity classes with appropriate JPA annotations Application Execution : Run the application to trigger the automatic analysis process SQL Autogeneration : The platform analyzes entity changes and generates SQL scripts in the hbm2ddl subdirectory Migration File Preparation : Move generated SQL files from hbm2ddl to the Flyway migration directory ( src/main/resources/db/migration/ ) File Naming : Rename files to follow Flyway convention: V{version}__{description}.sql Flyway Execution : During application startup, Flyway executes pending migrations in version order Schema Versioning : Database schema version is tracked automatically in the schema_version table Best Practices Incremental Changes : Create separate migration files for each schema change Descriptive Names : Use clear, descriptive names for migration files Testing : Test migrations on development environments bef

text: Core IT solutions for credit providers | Bankish Solutions About us Insights News room Case studies Blog Partners Contacts Schedule a demo Solutions built around how real lenders operate Bankish is an end-to-end loan management platform that helps financial institutions launch, run, and scale credit products with full control. Our modular system supports every step of the lending lifecycle, from onboarding to repayments, and adapts to a wide range of lending models. SEE ALL FEATURES Easily onboard clients through multiple channels Applications can be submitted via a self-service portal, physical office, website, or API-integrated partner systems. New products can be created and configured quickly, enabling a fast go-to-market strategy Flexible risk decisionin Support for fully automated and manual underwriting flows. Integrates with third-party data providers for credit checks and scoring. Loan agreements are generated automatically through a configurable approval process with full API access. Smart contract management and customer interaction Contracts and client data are easy to manage and search. All communication is logged in a centralized module, with smooth interaction between internal teams and the self-service portal. Automated email/SMS notifications are built in, and payment handling supports both manual and automated processes. Keep overdue payments under control Automated reminders via SMS and email help reduce delinquency. Late fees and penalty interest are calculated automatically to streamline recovery efforts. Insights for compliance, control, and growth Automatically generate profit & loss statements, portfolio overviews, and regulatory reports. Customizable templates support both internal and external reporting needs, including FCA and other regulatory standards. Serving modern lenders with full portfolio flexibility Whether you’re offering SME credit, consumer loans, leasing, or deposits — Bankish supports your operations with scalable, modular software tailored to lending. Flexible products and scoring for all needs Become the go-to financier in your field with Bankish. Maintain full control over your portfolio in real-time, be it by offering bespoke solutions for your key accounts or launching a completely new product category altogether. Remain on top of risk management with Bankish’s built-in scoring – run designated models for each product and override calculations, if necessary. Built for lenders of every size, with full credit portfolio coverage Bankish supports a wide range of lending models, from secured and unsecured loans to SME credit, microfinance, leasing, and deposits. Whether you’re launching a single product or managing a complex portfolio, the platform adapts to your needs with flexible modules, smart automation, and real-time control. All your lending tools in one flexible, scalable platform Product management Full control over your entire portfolio, to the detail. Easily launch or amend products by defining them using drop-down menus – from schedule types to transaction orders, from min-max definitions to fees’ management. Loans Full functionality coverage for the entire credit spectrum, regardless of the type or function. Unsecured and secured, business and consumer credit – Bankish is a single tool to cover it all, from origination to reporting. Deposits Manage deposits or inbound investments with our deposit module functionality. With both time and demand deposit coverage, Bankish supports funding operations of any financial institution. CRM Bankish features a comprehensive integral CRM to help maintain control over the business. Other than maintaining customer profiles, communications and contracts, the functionality enables automated messaging as well as internal tasks. Scoring With Bankish’s integral scoring engine, you can run designated risk models for each of your products. If desired, pre-, personal and credit scoring can be run separately to save on operational costs. Payments Payouts and collections are managed and coordinated in Bankish, from where outbound payments are initiated and incoming payments are allocated – both ISO-standard payment slips as well as direct gateway requests. Arrears management Delays and overdues are managed in Bankish with instant overview of arrears, by contract, by customer or by product. With high-detail views and process automation, debt management is a breeze with Bankish. Regulatory compliance All data is secured in a dedicated server instance and can be withdrawn by Bankish’s integral reporting functionality. In addition to standard accounting and regulatory reports, Bankish features a powerful BI solution. Why choose Bankish for your core-IT? Modular software Tailored solutions for credit providers from our full functionality stack – use what you need and scale how you want, today and tomorrow. End-to-end coverage Full product spectrum and life cycles’ coverage makes Bankish’s implementation the last transformation project your business needs to tend to. SaaS approach Affordable software rent and maintenance guaranteed from day 1 – Pay-as-you-Grow pricing model means you pay more only when you earn more. Your one-stop-shop core-IT with the help of our partners Our software is deliberately focused on credit provision and deposits, without “inventing the wheel” in ID verification, PSD2 or card-provision services, for instance. Bankish has a vibrant partner ecosystem ensuring end-to-end delivery for all your needs, collectively forming a true one-stop-shop for financial institutions. He’s also an underwriter with more than two decades’ experience, first at Euler, then at Hiscox for 15 years, then for four years as Underwriting Director at the MGA White Oak. In that last job he wanted to buy-in a decent underwriting platform, but couldn’t find a supplier who understood what an underwriter really needs, day to day. But he had learned some coding at college, so he built a platform himself to do the job, sold it, launched Quotech, and the rest is history. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to understand insurance business processes and the sector’s complex value chain like a native, then build systems which remove the inherent inefficiencies, not through chuck-it-all-out-and-start again approach, but incrementally. Follow Follow Marco Seoane Senior Software Developer Marco Seoane is Quotech’s front-end man, a Senior Software Developer with five years in the game, most of it with RecTech and MarTech early-stage B2B SaaS companies (before he found his home in insurTech, obviously). Marco says the best part about working in tech is that jeans and a t-shirt are acceptable workplace attire, but then his office is anywhere in London with an internet connection and a decent coffee. Give him those two, and he’ll get busy building and creating. “Idle hands are the devil’s workshop,” Marco says, as he pushes towards his self-imposed Friday production. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is all about reducing the cost of recording, managing, aggregating, and communicating about data, both cognitively and operationally. Follow Follow Lee John Martin Senior Software Developer Lee John Martin is Quotech’s main backend engineer (but claims “enough infrastructure and frontend knowledge to get myself into trouble”). A former graphic designer, he worked in insurTech for a year before joining Quotech, but during nearly a decade developing has built a geospatial SaaS tool in the property sector, an order-processing tool for a major consumer products supplier, and contract management software for the engineering sector, among many others. A man who prefers marathon running to commuting (he’s done 10 big jogs, last count), Lee delivers for Quotech customers from a box-room in his home in Gloucestershire with a black cat called Bobs (short for Bobbie, short for Roberta). Lee says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to get in your user’s head. You have to understand the user’s problem to solve it properly. And, he says, smart, simple ways of solving people’s problems are usually doable, and go well beyond what they think is possible. Follow Follow Niall Grant Senior Software Engineer Niall Grant is Senior Software Engineer at Quotech. His specialist areas are early-stage product development, backend APIs, command-line interfaces, databases, and system integrations – all of which means he has very particular skills. He’s deployed them over 18 years to build tools for sectors including HR, cloud operations, consulting, gambling, enterprise sales, and coaching. Every project is fuelled by his love of making stuff that has a meaningful, positive impact on the working lives of others – which is just what we like to do at Quotech. He does all this from his office in Edinburgh, where, for a different kind of positive impact, he’s a volunteer helmsman on the Lifeboats. In all this he is observed by his Working Cocker Spaniel, Flo, who Niall attests “has never worked a day in her life.” Niall says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to understand the challenges clients face, then build the right abstractions to enable business process flexibility, surface useful data and information to inform decision makers, and get new features to market quickly. Follow Follow Chris Pickford Product Manager Chris Pickford is Quotech’s Product Manager. He moved here to insurTech after eight years spent testing critical systems developed for accountancy. Eastbourne is his home by the sea, where he and Maisie, his Staffie, go where the connection is best to ensure everything works as it should for Quotech clients. “Being a start-up allows us to focus on any issues we face quickly and efficiently,” Chris says, “which helps us find the best way to work, and lets us create amazing solutions to any issues our clients face.” He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is building insurTech software that’s intuitive for users, and creating easier ways of working to make sure the major pain points no longer exist. Follow Follow Daniel Loader Lead Platform Engineer Daniel Loader is Quotech’s Lead Platform Engineer. He’s spent nearly a decade honing his craft in diverse sectors stretching from groceries to cyber security, working for household names like Iceland and Nominet. Now he’s made the crossing to insurance. From his home office in Manchester he works his magic for Quotech clients, with limited support from his cat Piggy and his tortoise González. His goal: to enable software engineers and ultimate users to work faster, with greater reliability, in part by deploying adjacent technology disciplines that provide the platform and services they need to succeed. Daniel says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to minimise users’ manual toil by making the workflow intuitive and the functionality smooth. Follow Follow Will Hunt Software Developer Will Hunt loves creative problem-solving. It’s the perfect predilection for a Quotech Software Developer. He does it in Go (the computer language), a skill he’s been perfecting over 11 years as a programmer, latterly for Sky. The best bit, he says, is the payoff: seeing something he’s built work better for users than they ever expected, making life easier for them. When he’s not coding from his front room in Plymouth, flanked by dogs Link and Apollo, cats Pixel and Artemis, a corn snake called Loki and a small sea’s worth of fish, Will is gaming or writing a science-fantasy novel. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to get feedback regularly from clients and users, measuring their requirements against your work. “You can’t get it right working in a vacuum,” he says. Follow Ezequiel Lopes Software Developer Ezequiel Lopes is an Argentinian from Bournemouth who studied CompSci in Portsmouth but grew up in Italy. We’re delighted he’s settled as a Software Developer at Quotech, where the positivity he brings to the team is as valuable as his intuitions as a front-end developer. He believes the best software comes from strong communication and shared understanding. A near-evangelical tech believer, he’s driven by the desire to simplify or automate to save precious time. Any he recoups for himself he spends playing basketball, Latin dancing, or adding to his list of 20 countries visited. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to understand the end user’s specific needs, make it intuitive and easy to use, and future-proof the app with scalability and flexibility. Follow Follow Ellen Daly Software Engineer Ellen Daly claims to be a life-long nerd at heart, so she fits right in as a Quotech Software Developer. Ellen loves problem-solving, and building things that help make people’s lives easier. She began her tech career as a UX researcher after a stint an academic researcher, then made the switch to development about two years ago. She’s never been happier in her work than now, she says! From her home office in a quiet Yorkshire village (complete with woodland view and golden retriever insatiable for belly rubs), Ellen works happily across the front- and back-ends, since that lets her get hands-on with the full picture. Ellen says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance – and what Quotech is really good at – is bridging the gap between what users need and what gets built. (That’s where, in former jobs, she’s seen many apps fall short.) The solution, she says, is to understand users deeply, and shape your solutions with them at the forefront. Follow Follow Esme Knight Software Developer Birmingham-based Esme Knight is a recreational climber who spends days surmounting challenges as a Quotech Software Developer. She’s perfect for the job, since she likes to get stuck into a problem. Give Esme a brief, and she will work out the detail of what’s needed from her very broad perspective: she injects working experience garnered over years in tech for automotive dealerships and in the TV, film, and theatre space. (Who wouldn’t give that up for insurance?) She loves the tech biz because every day’s a school day, but she keeps the arts close to her heart. Esme says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is the same as it is for any other industry: know the domain, which means you’re forced to keep asking questions. Esme’s questions come from a desk wedged into a corner of her living room. Follow Follow Rosa Catena Associate Product Manager Rosa Catena , Associate Product Manager at Quotech, lives in Staffordshire under the shadow of Alton Towers. With nearly a decade of tech experience under her belt, she switched to insurance from creating online buying journeys for the automotive industry. She’s an Italian on paper, but raised in Switzerland, and somehow has French as her strongest language (second to English). Her office is anywhere with strong Wi-Fi and strong coffee, and hopefully a dog (she has a crazy border collie called Luna). She likes Quotech because she can make positive, crucial changes, and is able to speak her mind in a shop that’s small enough for everyone’s voice to matter, but serious enough about the problem that the work feels real. Rosa says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is trust. It is essential to instil trust in end-users, she says, to make their journey seamless. Follow Follow Tanith Rietti Lead Quality Assurance Engineer Tanith Rietti is Quotech’s Quality Assurance Specialist, which is a polite way of saying she’s paid to break things before clients can. With more than 15 years in technology behind her, she has a knack for finding the one path through an application that nobody thought to test. She has a conviction that the fast pace and constant problem-solving of her work are exactly what make it worth doing (and who could argue?). Before she found her way into technology for insurance, Tanith sharpened her instincts across e-commerce and the jewellery trade, two worlds where the details really do matter. Meanwhile Tanith is a committed advocate for women in tech and for neurodiversity, and brings her spirit of championing others to the team. Tanith says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is simple to state but hard to achieve: understand the users and the industry, and everything else follows. At Quotech, the friendly, collaborative, and “genuinely in it together” culture make that easier, she says. Follow Follow Alex Mills Senior Platform Engineer Alex Mills , Senior Platform Engineer at Quotech, has worked in technology for 17 years, but he still finds real satisfaction in taking something people dread to use and transforming it into something they don’t need to think about. To do that, he digs deep into problems, usually by asking “why” more times than is strictly comfortable. He came to insurance without the industry’s embedded assumptions, so he asks often. That turns out to matter more than you might think. He solves technology challenges from his home in Droitwich, which he describes as “somewhat over-engineered” due to his Wallace-like automation of things that absolutely did not need it. Plus, it’s a menagerie, shared with Moscow and Wilson (former racehorses), Shiny and Strawberry (goldfish), and Molly the cat. Remaining time is spent away from the screen with family (mostly, when he’s not playing D&D with childhood friends, or tracking aircraft). Alex says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to build something that fits that workflow, rather than fights with it. The best software removes steps. It never adds a system that busy people have to feed. It also has to be transparent, because no one will stake a risk decision on a black box. Follow Follow Meet the team. What is Genasys and what does it do? Genasys is cloud-based insurance software that brings policy administration , claims management and billing together in a single platform. It is built for insurers, MGAs and brokers managing delegated authority, with no-code product building tools, 350+ pre-configured templates and 450+ documented API endpoints . Genasys is headquartered in London with offices in South Africa, and has been serving the insurance industry for nearly 30 years. The platform is used by enterprise carriers transacting hundreds of millions in GWP and scaling MGAs launching new products in days. Genasys has been recognised by Celent, CNBC & Statista and BusinessCloud as one of the leading insurance technology platforms in the world. How long does implementation take, and how disruptive is migration from our legacy system? Implementation timelines depend on product complexity, integrations and data migration scope, but the platform is configured rather than heavily customised, which reduces delivery risk and time. Genasys delivered Arma Karma's policy administration platform in one week and King Price migrated from legacy technology in six weeks , though more complex environments will naturally take longer. Migration is handled through structured data import routines and reconciliation checks to ensure accuracy, with the option to phase deployment by product, entity or distribution channel. This staged approach allows organisations to transition gradually and avoid operational disruption during the move from legacy systems. What types of insurance business does Genasys support? Genasys is used by insurers, MGAs, brokers and third-party administrators across personal, commercial and specialty lines. The platform supports complex insurance structures including multi-currency, multi-jurisdictional tax, co-insurance, capacity splits and delegated authority arrangements. Customers range from startup MGAs launching their first product to established carriers managing large, complex books across multiple regions. Current clients include Simplyhealth, King Price , Hamilton, Guardrisk, Arma Karma , CTU and BSpoke Group, among others. How does Genasys integrate with our existing technology ecosystem? Genasys is built on an open API architecture with more than 450 documented RESTful API endpoints . External systems can create, read and update platform data across policy , claims and billing modules. This enables integration with pricing engines, CRM systems, general ledgers, premium finance providers, data enrichment services, payment platforms and distribution channels. Genasys also supports real-time eventing and automated B2B data feeds, removing the need for manual bordereaux processing. Clients retain their existing technology ecosystem while using Genasys as the core operational system. What does it actually cost, and how does total cost of ownership compare to legacy platforms? Pricing is based on factors including users, transaction volumes, integrations and migration scope. title: From AI Proof of Concept to Production: What changes
description: Moving an AI proof of concept into production adds eight things around an unchanged model. What they are, the cost, and how to define the finish line.
text: From AI Proof of Concept to Production: What changes Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Services Inspire AI Demo AI Webinar Hire an AI Speaker Learn AI Training AI Workshop AI Hackathon Advise AI Consulting AI Strategy AI Assessment Create Hire an AI Team Proof of Concept AI Development & Implementation Compensate your CO2 Compensate the CO2 usage of AI solutions with DataNorth and Trees for All Solutions Case Studies About About About DataNorth Working at DataNorth News Blog Downloads Contact us Be part of the team! We understand that our solutions will have real-world implications for our planet. What changes is everything around it: exception handling, a human review step, a test set with an acceptance bar, monitoring, access control and logging, a fallback path, a named owner with time, and a support arrangement with a known cost. That ring is the work, and it is where the budget goes. Teams are consistently surprised by this, because a PoC answers a different question than production does. A PoC asks whether the model can produce the right answer. Production asks whether the surrounding system can handle the wrong one safely, at volume, on a Tuesday, when the person who built it is on holiday. The gap is now the defining problem in enterprise AI. Deloitte surveyed more than three thousand leaders across twenty-four countries for its 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise report and found that twenty-three percent use agentic AI at least moderately today while seventy-four percent expect to within two years, yet only twenty-one percent have a mature governance model for those agents. The ambition is running well ahead of the operating capability, and the space between the two is exactly what this article covers. Why does a proof of concept not become production by itself? Because the two are optimised for opposite things. A PoC is built to answer a question quickly, so it runs on sample data, gets invoked by hand, lives in a demo environment and depends on the person who made it. Every one of those shortcuts is correct at the time and every one of them has to be removed before anything real depends on the output. That gap is where most projects end. RAND interviewed sixty-five experienced data scientists and engineers for its study on the root causes of failure for AI projects and found that more than eighty percent fail, roughly twice the rate of comparable IT projects, with deployment infrastructure treated as an afterthought among the main causes. Gartner expects more than forty percent of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027 , naming escalating costs first. Both point at the same place: the ring around the model. The second reason is that the exceptions were not in the sample. A PoC is usually tested on the cases somebody could easily assemble, which skews towards the ordinary ones. Production traffic contains the document with two invoices in one PDF, the order that arrived without a reference number, the record where a field that is always filled is empty. In our own document processing work the pattern is consistent: the straightforward path is quick to build, and the last stretch of accuracy comes entirely from handling the awkward cases. A recent example from our own practice makes the shape of it concrete. On a purchase invoice automation project we benchmarked a full year of invoices, roughly seven thousand of them, and reached eighty-eight percent straight-through processing, with the invoices that carried no annotation booked to the right ledger account against booking history in ninety-three and a half percent of cases. Those are good numbers, and the system was still not in production, because at that point nothing had been written back into the financial system. Accuracy was never the constraint. The write-back, the review step and the permissions were. What actually gets added in production? Eight things, and none of them is the model. Exception handling comes first because it is the largest. Decide what happens when confidence is low, when a required field is missing, when an upstream system is unavailable. In most business processes this logic is bigger than the AI component, and it is what separates a system people trust from one they check behind. A human review step needs a place and a person, not a principle. Where in the flow does the human see the output, what can they change, and what happens to their correction? A correction that disappears is a missed opportunity, because the same corrections repeated are the cheapest training data you will ever get. A test set with an acceptance bar turns “it seems to work” into a number you can defend. Assemble real cases with known correct answers, including the hard ones, and state the threshold before you measure rather than after. Monitoring and alerting answers a question nobody asks until it matters: how would you know if this stopped working? Silent failure is the characteristic failure mode of AI systems, because they keep producing confident output after the input has changed underneath them. Access control and logging covers which accounts the system uses, what it may read and write, and what record exists of what it did. This is also where regulatory obligations land, so it is worth aligning with the risk class established during preparation rather than retrofitting. A fallback path is the manual route people take when the system is down. If nobody has defined it, the fallback is improvisation, and improvisation during an incident is how data gets lost. An owner with time allocated is the condition most often assumed rather than arranged. Somebody has to decide about changes, exceptions and priorities after go-live, and if that is nobody’s job it becomes the developer’s, which is how teams end up unable to start anything new. A support arrangement with a known cost makes the running commitment explicit. What is covered, what response time applies, and what it costs per month. Without it, maintenance gets done informally until it quietly stops being done at all. How do you know when you are actually finished? When the process being replaced can be switched off. That bar is deliberately harder than “the system works”, and it is the only one that prevents the outcome where a new system runs alongside the old way indefinitely, costing more than either option on its own. It also makes prioritisation straightforward, because it converts a feature wishlist into four ordered buckets. On the invoice project above we sorted the client’s requested features exactly that way: what already worked, what was needed in this phase, what could wait a quarter, and what we recommended against building at all. Of the features in the current phase, we marked which ones specifically blocked switching off the legacy tool, and those became the definition of finished. The three we advised against, including splitting multiple invoices out of a single PDF, were genuine requests that would have cost more than the manual handling they replaced. That last category matters more than it sounds. Saying no to a feature the client asked for is uncomfortable, and it is often the difference between reaching production this quarter and reaching it next year. What does it cost to keep running? Three components, and organisations tend to misjudge two of them in opposite directions. Cloud and model consumption is routinely overestimated. On one recent project the client had budgeted roughly two hundred euros a month for the infrastructure and our engineer estimated about sixty, because the workload was event-driven rather than continuously running. That difference is architectural rather than negotiable: a workflow triggered by incoming documents costs a fraction of a service that polls all day. It is worth checking this assumption early, because inflated running-cost estimates have killed business cases that were actually sound. Maintenance hours are routinely underestimated. Changes arrive because the world changes: a supplier alters a document layout, a system gets upgraded, a rule changes. A reasonable planning figure is a modest number of hours a month at a normal engineering rate, and the honest version of that conversation happens before go-live rather than at the first invoice. Coordination is the part nobody budgets. As a rule of thumb we allow around ten percent of development effort for project management, and something similar applies after launch for the smaller matter of who decides what when an exception pattern shows up. What rhythm gets a build across the line? Short cycles with the people who will use the system, rather than milestone reviews with the people who approved it. The pattern that works for us is a weekly demo throughout the build. On a customer-facing assistant we delivered last year, the shape was a forty-hour proof of concept followed by ten weekly sprint demos, after which the assistant went live in production on WhatsApp Business. Ten demos sounds like a lot of meetings and it is considerably cheaper than the alternative, which is discovering in week nine that the tone of voice is wrong or that a whole category of question was out of scope. Weekly also changes who attends. A monthly steering review attracts managers, while a weekly demo attracts the people who do the work, and they are the ones who spot that the output is technically correct but arrives in the wrong place in their day. What should the handover cover? More than most contracts specify, which is why it is worth agreeing explicitly rather than assuming. Source code, prompts and documentation are the obvious components, and a short review before transfer is sensible so that what arrives is usable rather than merely complete. Beyond that, three things need a decision. Whether repository history and logs transfer, which is often outside standard scope and comes as a surprise if nobody asked. Where the system will run afterwards, since a solution handed over as source code moves onto the client’s own infrastructure and any hosting arrangement becomes a separate question. And who holds the credentials, because an application nobody can authenticate into is not really handed over. The test for a complete handover is simple: could a competent engineer who has never seen this system deploy it, run it and fix a common failure using only what you provided? If the honest answer needs a phone call to the original developer, the handover is not finished. The shortest useful summary A proof of concept answers whether something is possible, and that question is usually settled within a few weeks. Everything after that is about making the answer dependable enough that a business process can lean on it, which is ordinary engineering work rather than AI work, and which is where the majority of the effort and nearly all of the surprises live. Budget accordingly. Treating the PoC as most of the project is the single most reliable way to end up in the group that never ships. Frequently asked questions (FAQ) about moving AI into production Why do AI proofs of concept fail to reach production? Because a PoC proves the model can produce the right answer, while production requires the surrounding system to handle wrong answers safely. Exception handling, monitoring, access control and ownership are usually deferred during the PoC and then discovered as a second project nobody budgeted for. How long does it take to move an AI PoC into production? For a scoped single-process use case, plan on eight to twelve weeks of iteration after the PoC. A useful rhythm is a weekly demo with the people who will actually use it, so scope and acceptance criteria get corrected while changes are still cheap. What does it cost to run an AI system after go-live? Budget three parts: cloud and model consumption, which is often tens of euros a month for an event-driven workflow rather than hundreds; maintenance hours for changes and incidents; and roughly ten percent of the original development effort for coordination. The first is usually overestimated and the second underestimated. When is an AI system genuinely in production? When the process it replaces can be switched off. That is a harder bar than “it works”, and it is the only one that prevents a system running in parallel with the old way indefinitely, which costs more than either option on its own. What should be handed over when a build finishes? Source code, prompts and documentation, plus a description of how to run and monitor the system. Agree explicitly whether repository history, logs and hosting transfer as well, because those are often outside the standard scope and the assumption gap surfaces at the worst moment. Hinweise zur Prüfung der Echtheit von Produktbewertungen Wir haben einige Maßnahmen ergriffen, um sicherzustellen, dass veröffentlichte Bewertungen nur von Kunden stammen, die die Produkte tatsächlich erworben haben. Diese Bewertungen werden als „verifizierter Kauf“ gekennzeichnet. Angemeldete BenutzterInnen haben im Kundenkonto die Möglichkeit, die Produkte vergangener Bestellungen zu bewerten. Zudem kann über Bewertungslinks in von uns oder von angeschlossenen Dienstleistern versendeten E-Mails Produkte bewertet werden. Dabei ist es technisch sichergestellt, dass nur die tatsächlich gekauften Produkte bewertet werden können. Zusätzlich gibt es die Möglichkeit, Produktbewertungen auf der Produktdetailseite abzugeben. Dabei wird technisch geprüft, ob der Artikel vom Benutzer gekauft wurde. Kann eine Verifizierung nicht automatisch durchgeführt werden, werden Bewertungen händisch geprüft und nur dann als verifiziert eingestuft, wenn ein tatsächlicher Kauf vorliegt. Kann nicht sicher gestellt werden, dass das Produkt auch tatsächlich gekauft wurde, wird die Bewertung nicht als „verifizierter Kauf“ gekennzeichnet. Zudem nutzen wir Trusted Shops als unabhängigen Dienstleister für die Einholung von Bewertungen. Gesammelt unter den Trusted Shops Nutzungsbedingungen . Über die Echtheit der Trusted Shops Bewertungen. Für ein optimales Einkaufserlebnis zeigen wir Bewertungen identischer Artikel an, die in den Shops angeschlossener Unternehmen getätigt wurden. Einige dieser Unternehmen holen über den unabhängigen Dienstleister WebwinkelKeur Bewertungen ein. WebwinkelKeur bittet per E-Mail um die Bewertung von Produkten, welche mit der Bestellung des Kunden von unseren Systemen übermittelt wurden. Somit wird gewährleistet, dass nur Produkte bewertet werden, die tatsächlich gekauft wurden. Weitere Informationen zur Produktbewertung von Webwinkelkeur . Seit mehr als einem Jahrhundert arbeiten unsere Mitarbeiter nahezu rund um die Uhr, um Sie beispielsweise im Einzelhandel, der Druckindustrie, im Lebensmittelumfeld oder die Gastronomie mit besten Papierprodukten zu versorgen. Wie wir das machen? Zum einen mit modernsten Spezialmaschinen für Schneide-, Druck- und Verpackungstechniken. Zum anderen mit einer stets großen Freude an dem, was wir tun. Dabei sind wir weder besonders laut, noch besonders leise – sondern einfach verbindlich. Und dazu multikulturell und fürsorglich zu Menschen mit Handicap. Das alles und eine Willkommens- und Unternehmenskultur, die weit über die Region hinaus bekannt ist, trägt sicher auch zur langen Betriebszugehörigkeit unserer 200 Mitarbeiter bei. Und produktseitig steht unser FSC®-Zertifikat für Glaubwürdigkeit, Transparenz und Verantwortungsbewusstsein. Wenn’s um Papierrollen geht, macht uns niemand was vor Flexibilität und Dynamik sind nur zwei Aspekte, auf die Sie sich bei uns verlassen können. Wenn Sie als Unternehmen der Druckindustrie, als industrieller Fertiger, als Einzelhändler oder als Systemgastronom – um nur einige zu nennen – zusätzlich noch Wert in Sachen Rollenpapier auf Kontinuität und eine verlässliche und wertschätzende Partnerschaft legen, treffen Sie mit uns eine gute Wahl. Wir übernehmen gern sämtliche Entwicklungs- und Serviceleistungen, realisieren die Produktion und versenden weltweit. Dass Sie sich mit uns für den denkbar versiertesten Dienstleister entschieden haben, erkennen Sie spätestens, wenn: Ihr Papier vollautomatisiert und damit effektiv vom Band läuft. Sie Ihre Sonderanfertigung maßgeschneidert von uns bekommen Sie aus einer Vielfalt an Materialien Ihr Wunschpapier wählen. Ihre Bestellung zum vereinbarten Lieferdatum bei Ihnen eintrifft. Wir Sonderwünsche unkompliziert auf einer Spezialmaschine umsetzen. Wir Ihnen unsere Schneidemaschinen mit integrierten 5-Farb-Druckwerken präsentieren. Sie die Qualität bei Auslieferung fühlen können. Sie sich über eine Rechnung mit fairen Preisen freuen. FSC®-Zertifiziert Glaubwürdigkeit und Transparenz spiegeln sich auch im FSC®-Zertifikat: Mit dem FSC®-Label auf den von uns ausgezeichneten Papierprodukten stehen wir ein für einen verantwortungsbewussten Umgang mit Ressourcen. Die Produktkettenzertifizierung garantiert in jeder Verarbeitungs- und Handelsstufe eindeutig identifizierbares Material aus nachhaltiger Waldwirtschaft. Sedex®-Mitglied Sedex (Supplier Ehtical Data Exchange) ist eine globale und gemeinnützige Mitglieder-Organisation für Unternehmen, die sich zu einer kontinuierlichen Verbesserung des ethischen Verhaltens in ihrer Lieferkette verpflichtet haben. Sedex ist eine international anerkannte Plattform, die das ethische Management von Lieferketten ermöglicht. Inzwischen hat die Organisation über 65.000 Mitglieder (Stand: Mitte 2022). text: Polleres Gruppe | Polleres Gruppe Über uns Team Philosophie Geschichte News Jobbörse Geschäftsfelder Polleres Malerbetrieb PVV Immobilien MGR Facility Services 3P Trockenbau Baumeister Vogler Polleres Plastic Kontakt Als Malerbetrieb gegründet, heute eine stolze Firmengruppe Mit Malerarbeiten, Facility Services, Trockenbau, Baumeisterei und Immobilienentwicklung hat die Polleres Gruppe ihren Schwerpunkt im Baugewerbe, bietet aber auch Tiefziehteile und Kunststoffverpackungen an. Mehr Liebe zum Handwerk, Freude an der Arbeit „Gern geschehen!“ So lautet unser Leitsatz. Denn was man gerne macht, macht man gut. Dass unsere Arbeit Qualität hat, liegt aber auch an Fachkompetenz, Leistungsfähigkeit und dem Selbstverständnis als Dienstleister. Mehr Immobilien in Mattersburg Unsere Immobilien werden in Handwerksqualität und mit erstklassigen, umweltfreundlichen Materialien errichtet bzw. saniert. Bei der Vermittlung der Objekte legen wir sehr viel Wert auf persönliche Betreuung und ein herausragendes Service. Unsere aktuellen Immobilienobjekte befinden sich direkt im Herzen von Mattersburg, da uns der Erhalt und die Belebung des Stadtzentrums besonders wichtig sind. Mehr Entdecken Sie die Vielfalt unserer Unternehmensgruppe Entdecken Sie die Vielfalt unserer Unternehmensgruppe » Mehr erfahren „Gern geschehen!“ Diesen Satz werden Sie öfter hören, wenn Sie mit uns oder einem unserer Unternehmen zu tun haben. Er bringt nicht nur unsere Liebe zum Handwerk und die Freude an der Arbeit auf den Punkt, er steht auch sinnbildlich für unser Selbstverständnis als Dienstleister. Wir beraten und unterstützen unseren Kundinnen und Kunden, wo wir können. Und wir helfen gerne mit vollem Einsatz mit, auch Ihre Vorstellungen und Wünsche zu erfüllen und in die Tat umzusetzen. Dabei achten wir stets auf höchste Qualität. Von der Planung bis zur Umsetzung. Denn wir wollen in jeder Hinsicht saubere Arbeit liefern. 1965 als Malerbetrieb begründet, haben wir heute mehrere Standbeine mit einem Schwerpunkt im Baugewerbe. So besteht die Polleres Gruppe aus insgesamt zehn Einzelunternehmen, die in den Geschäftsfeldern Malerei, Facility Services, Trockenbau, Baumeisterei, Immobilienentwicklung und Kunststoffverarbeitung tätig sind. Rund 300 Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeitern zeugen nicht nur von unserer Leistungsstärke, sie machen uns auch zu einem der wichtigsten Arbeitgeber der Region. Kein Auftrag zu gross, keine Aufgabe zu klein Polleres Malerbetrieb Mit rund 130 Mitarbeitern und Standorten im Burgenland, in Wien und Niederösterreich sind wir einer der größten Malerbetriebe der Ostregion und der richtige Partner für große wie kleine Maler-, Tapezierer- und Bodenlegerarbeiten. Immobilien in Handwerksqualität PVV Immobilien Gemeinsam mit den Unternehmen unserer Firmengruppe und langjährigen Partnern entwickeln wir Häuser und Wohnungen zum Wohlfühlen. Dabei legen wir Wert auf eine hochwertige Ausführung und ein großartiges Service. Ihre Aufgabe in guten Händen MGR Facility Services Mit rund 60 Mitarbeitern übernehmen wir alle Aufgaben des Facility Managements rund um Ihre Immobilie und Liegenschaft: von Reinigungsarbeiten über technische Dienstleistungen bis zum Gebäudemanagement. Professionell, pünktlich, perfekt = 3P 3P Trockenbau Wir übernehmen alle Arbeiten im Innenausbau und Trockenbau im öffentlichen wie privaten Bereich. Dabei legen wir im Sinn der 3P Wert auf professionelle Planung, pünktliche Fertigstellung und perfekte Ausführung. Ihr kompetenter Partner in allen Baufragen Baumeister Vogler Mit rund 20 Mitarbeitern sind wir das richtige Unternehmen für Bauprojekte aller Art. Dabei verbinden wir handwerkliche Tradition mit modernsten Verarbeitungsmethoden, innovativen Technologien und ökologischem Bauen. Tiefziehteile aus Kunststoff in Bestform Polleres Plastic Kunststoffverarbeitung Wir gehören zu den modernsten Herstellern von tiefgezogenen Kunststoffteilen im Food- und Nonfood-Bereich und bieten auch individuelle Lösungen für Verpackungen, Werkstückträger, Transporttrays oder andere Produkte. Die 1965 von KR Johann Polleres begründete Polleres Gruppe wird von Mag. Judith Polleres-Vogler geleitet und zählt insgesamt rund 300 Beschäftigte. Grâce à une sélection rigoureuse de solutions adaptées à chaque activité , nous vous aidons à optimiser vos expéditions, vos flux logistiques et vos ventes en point de vente. ... Quel que soit votre métier, nos produits vous permettent d’atteindre vos objectifs : gain de temps, de place, de productivité, mais aussi meilleure sécurité pour vos collaborateurs et vos marchandises. Nos experts vous conseillent et vous orientent vers les références les plus adaptées à votre besoin spécifique. Emballez mieux, plus vite, plus efficacement : optimisez chaque étape avec Cenpac, votre partenaire en emballages et équipements professionnels . Découvrez nos gammes d’emballages et d’équipements professionnels En tant que fournisseur d’emballages et d’équipements professionnels , nous vous proposons une offre complète couvrant tous les types d’emballages : papier , plastique , sacs , pochettes , solutions de cerclage , protection , équipements et consommables pour la manutention, le stockage ou encore l’hygiène. Chaque univers est pensé pour répondre aux enjeux spécifiques de votre quotidien. Emballages alimentaires Optimisez la présentation et la conservation de vos denrées avec notre gamme de papiers alimentaires , d’ emballages boucherie , d’ emballages alimentaires personnalisés ou encore de boîtes isothermes pour transport alimentaire . Pour les professionnels de la vente à emporter ou les primeurs, retrouvez également nos emballages pour pâtisseries , sacs plastiques alimentaires , emballages à fruits , emballages pour bouteilles , équipements d’hygiène alimentaire et emballages sous vide . Pensez aussi à notre sélection dédiée à la vente à emporter . Caisses et cartons Simples, doubles ou triples cannelures, formats standards ou personnalisés : nos caisses carton permettent de protéger efficacement vos marchandises pendant le transport ou le stockage. Boîtes, pochettes et étiquettes Découvrez notre gamme de boîtes postales, étuis, pochettes et étiquettes pour expédier vos produits avec fiabilité, tout en valorisant votre image de marque. Adhésifs, colles et liens Pour une fermeture sécurisée de tous vos colis, choisissez parmi nos rubans adhésifs, colles techniques, liens métalliques ou plastiques, avec ou sans système de dévidoir. Films et housses palettes Stabilisez vos palettes et protégez vos produits grâce à notre gamme de films étirables, rétractables ou préétirés, manuels ou automatiques. Calage et protection Maîtrisez les chocs, vibrations et risques de casse avec des solutions de calage en papier, mousse, coussins d’air ou carton alvéolaire. Cerclage et agrafage Assurez un maintien optimal de vos colis ou palettes avec des feuillards en PP, PET ou acier, accompagnés de chapes, tendeurs ou agrafeuses professionnelles. Sacherie et conditionnement Polyéthylène, kraft, à soufflets, à zip ou à fond carton : trouvez le sac qui convient à votre usage, qu’il soit alimentaire, industriel ou promotionnel. Manutention et stockage Optimisez vos flux logistiques avec des solutions de stockage robustes, des caisses plastiques, des bacs gerbables ou encore des chariots de manutention. Machines et systèmes d’emballage Accélérez vos opérations d’emballage grâce à nos machines de cerclage, soudeuses, filmeuses automatiques et tables de conditionnement. Hygiène et entretien Préservez la propreté de vos locaux et le confort de vos équipes avec notre offre de produits d’entretien, de nettoyage, de désinfection et de protections individuelles. Sacs Du sac kraft au sac cabas en passant par les sacs recyclables , cette gamme complète répond à tous vos besoins en conditionnement léger ou en communication point de vente. Pourquoi choisir Cenpac comme fournisseur d’emballages et d’équipements professionnels ? Nous proposons une gamme complète de produits pour répondre à tous les besoins, en intégrant les standards de qualité et les dernières innovations du marché. Nos solutions sont conçues pour garantir la sécurité de vos marchandises, améliorer votre productivité et valoriser votre image de marque. Grâce à notre équipe d’experts terrain et sédentaires, vous bénéficiez d’un accompagnement sur-mesure tout au long de votre chaîne logistique. En tant que fournisseur d’emballages et d’équipements professionnels , notre engagement est clair : vous fournir des produits fiables, disponibles et efficaces, qui vous permettent de gagner en performance au quotidien. Quelle que soit la nature de votre produit, nous avons la solution adaptée, prête à créer de la valeur pour votre entreprise. Des solutions globales qui font la différence En choisissant Cenpac comme fournisseur d'emballages et d’équipements professionnels , vous avez accès à : Des produits disponibles en stock, sélectionnés pour leur fiabilité, Des références adaptées à chaque type de produit : alimentaire, industriel, fragile, lourd, etc., Des emballages recyclables en papier ou en plastique , Des conseils personnalisés pour optimiser vos flux logistiques, Un service client réactif et à l’écoute, Une expertise métier reconnue dans tout le secteur de l’emballage et des équipements professionnels. Quel que soit le volume ou la complexité de vos besoins, nous avons les produits et le savoir-faire qui vous permettent d’ajouter de la valeur à chaque étape de votre chaîne logistique. Cenpac, votre partenaire d'emballages et équipements professionnels Que vous recherchiez des sacs en papier, des films étirables, des machines d’emballage ou des solutions de cerclage , Cenpac est le fournisseur d'emballages et d’équipements professionnels sur lequel vous pouvez compter. Sí. YM Packaging Group diseña y fabrica maquinaria de packaging y de envasado en Elche (Alicante): envasadoras verticales, horizontales y flowpack, pesadoras, control de calidad, encajado, paletizado y líneas completas. ¿Dónde está YM Packaging? Somos fabricantes de maquinaria de envasado en España, con sede en Elche (Alicante), y tenemos oficinas en el Reino Unido (Manchester) y en China (Guangzhou). ¿Fabricáis maquinaria de packaging para monodosis? Sí. La envasadora de sachet y stick trabaja con 1 a 12 pistas y hasta 300 sticks por minuto, con dosis de 3 a 50 ml. Para monodosis en bolsa preformada a alta velocidad está la EPX 120 ML. ¿Fabricáis líneas de envasado completas? Sí. Integramos dosificación, envasado, control de calidad, encajado y paletizado en una línea llave en mano con un solo proveedor. ¿Sois proveedores de maquinaria para ensacado en España? Sí. Fabricamos ensacadoras para sacos de gran formato, como la EVR 1100 (sacos de hasta 480 mm de ancho), y nos encargamos de la instalación y del servicio técnico. ¿Trabajáis con empresas de embalaje industrial y de envasado a terceros? Sí. Configuramos máquinas que admiten varios productos, envases y formatos, que es lo que necesita una empresa que envasa para distintas marcas. ¿Ofrecéis servicio técnico y mantenimiento? Sí. Nuestro equipo técnico se encarga de la instalación, la puesta en marcha y el mantenimiento de la maquinaria para minimizar las paradas de producción. Leer artículo Fabricantes de maquinaria packaging en España YM Packaging Group es fabricante de envasadoras en España . Diseñamos, fabricamos, instalamos y mantenemos maquinaria de envasado y de embalaje para la industria alimentaria y no alimentaria desde nuestra sede en Elche (Alicante), con oficinas en el Reino Unido (Manchester) y en China (Guangzhou). Nuestro sistema de calidad está certificado ISO 9001:2015 por SGS. Como fabricantes de maquinaria de envasado desde hace más de 15 años, conocemos cada etapa de la producción: el dosificado, el envasado, el control de calidad, el encajado y el paletizado. Conoce la empresa . Fabricantes de maquinaria de embalaje para cada etapa Somos fabricantes de maquinaria de embalaje y de envasado para el envasado primario y el secundario. Estas son las familias de máquinas de envasado que fabricamos: Envasadoras verticales : de 40 a 240 bolsas/min. Envasadoras horizontales y máquinas doypack : hasta 400 bolsas/min. Envasadoras flowpack : hasta 80 bolsas/min y bobinas de hasta 1000 mm. Pesadoras multicabezales y llenadoras de botes . Control de calidad : detectores de metales y controladoras de peso. Final de línea: encajado y paletizado , con formadoras de cajas, precintadoras, paletizadores y robots. Fabricantes de maquinaria packaging monodosis Para sobres monodosis fabricamos la envasadora de sachet y stick : forma, llena y cierra sachets y sticks desde bobina, en versiones de 1 a 12 pistas y hasta 300 sticks por minuto, con dosis de 3 a 50 ml de polvo, líquido, granulado o sólido. Para monodosis en bolsa preformada a alta velocidad está la EPX 120 ML . Más información sobre las envasadoras de sachet y el envase stick . Fabricantes de maquinaria para líneas de envasado Además de máquinas sueltas, somos fabricantes de maquinaria para líneas de envasado completas: integramos dosificación, envasado, control de calidad, encajado y paletizado en una sola línea y con un solo proveedor. Dos ejemplos: la línea de envasado de hielo y la línea de envasado de proteína en polvo . Ver las líneas completas llave en mano . Proveedor de maquinaria para ensacado en España Para sacos de gran formato somos proveedor de maquinaria para ensacado en España . Nuestras ensacadoras forman, llenan y cierran el saco desde bobina, en almohadilla o con fondo plano, y dosifican con pesadora multicabezal o lineal. Se usan para harinas, piensos, sal, legumbres o productos congelados. La ensacadora EVR 1100 hace sacos de hasta 480 mm de ancho con bobina de hasta 1000 mm y es más baja que otras ensacadoras, así el producto cae desde menos altura y llega entero al saco. Maquinaria para empresas de embalaje industrial Trabajamos con fabricantes de alimentación y con empresas de embalaje industrial y de envasado a terceros , que envasan productos de distintas marcas en la misma planta. Para ellas, la maquinaria para empresa de embalaje tiene que admitir varios productos, envases y formatos, así que elegimos el dosificador y la envasadora para cada caso y planificamos los cambios de formato desde el estudio inicial. Cómo trabajamos Estudio. Analizamos tu producto, tu envase, tu producción y el espacio de tu planta. Diseño a medida. Elegimos y configuramos cada máquina, o la línea completa llave en mano , del dosificado al palé. Fabricación e instalación. Fabricamos, probamos y ponemos en marcha la maquinaria en tu planta. Servicio técnico. Nuestro equipo de mantenimiento cuida de tus equipos para que no se pare la producción. Cuéntanos tu proyecto y te proponemos la solución. På vores lager har vi et bredt sortiment af udstyr til løft, så der er god mulighed for at finde det helt rigtige løftegrej til de forskellige erhverv. Har vi ikke det specifikke på lager, kan vi med fordel producere det til dig på vores eget riggerværksted. Find det helt rigtige løftegrej! Vi står klar til at hjælpe dig med din næste opgave. Vi kan bl.a. levere stålwire, løftegrej og surring. Anvendelse af vores produkter spænder fra undervandsbrug til løft af vindmøller og andre tunge emner. Vi bestræber os altid på at levere produkter af højeste kvalitet. Vi leverer også altid fleksible løsninger til dit erhverv, uanset hvilken løfteopgave du har brug for hjælp til. Et sikkert løft er altid vores første prioritet, og derfor står vi til rådighed for dig, når du har brug for en ekspert, der har stor knowhow inden for løfteudstyr. NOS er blevet kendt for at kunne tilføje den nødvendige ekstra værdi for kunderne, i form af; Rådgivning, årlige eftersyn af løftegrej og surring, belastningsprøver af kraner, løfteåg mv., montage og vedligehold, udlejning af udstyr, samt lagerhotel. Så kort og godt: ”VI ER HER FOR JER!” NOS A/S - Sætter kunden i fokus Når du vælger os, er du sikker på en solid samarbejdspartner med mange års erfaring. Vi er en forholdsvis lille virksomhed, og derfor er vores kunder altid i centrum. Hvis der skulle opstå problemer, reagerer vi hurtigt og fleksibelt, for vi ved, at det koster dyrt, når produktionen forsinkes. Ring til os – vi kan med garanti også hjælpe dig! NOS er blevet kendt for at kunne tilføje den nødvendige ekstraværdi for kunderne i form af rådgivning, årlige eftersyn af surringer og løftegrej, belastningsprøver af kraner, løfteåg mv. samt montage og vedligehold. Vi kommer ud og tester, om produkterne overholder de lovmæssige krav. Vi kigger blandt andet på stålwirer, surring og løftegrej. Her kan du få et overblik over de forskellige former for løfteudstyr, som vi forhandler: Stålwirer Sjækler Øjebolte Tovværk Løfteåg Surringer Kædetaljer Meget andet … Professionel rådgivning Vi giver dig også gerne råd og vejledning om alt inden for løfteudstyr til industri, kran, betonelementer, plader, så du får de rigtig stålwirer, løfteåg, båndstropper og andet tilbehør. Er du interesseret i at vide, hvordan man måler, hvor meget en stålwire kan klare? Eller vil du have hjælp til hvilke fastspændingsmetoder, der passer til forskellige surringsprodukter? Så står vi klar med vores viden og erfaring inden for løfteudstyr, så du kan få den mest effektive løsning med hjem. Anker, ankerkæder & tilbehør Løftekæder & tilbehør – klasse 8 Kædetaljer, spil, løfteklør & magneter Dynamometre & vandsække Stålwirer & tilbehør Tovværk & tilbehør Se vores produkt oversigt 24 timers service: Du kan altid få hjælp Hos os tilbyder vi personlig service 24 timer i døgnet. Vi ved, hvor vigtigt det er, at alt spiller. Og hvis det ikke gør, sørger vi for at være til stede – så det hurtigt kommer til at køre på skinner igen. Vi har ofte kunder fra nærområdet ved Horsens, Hedensted, Vejle, Silkeborg og Århus – men vi er meget fleksible og dækker hele Danmark, så tøv ikke med at kontakte os uanset geografi. Vi har også vores eget riggerværksted , hvor vi bl.a. håndsplejser stålwirer, taifuner, trosser og lignende. Så hvis du står og mangler speciallavede produkter, kan vi klare det for dig. Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig. text: Leichtbau: Leichtbauteile Hersteller Oberösterreich - TRIPAN Leichtbauteile de en Leichtbau Dienstleistungen Kernmaterialien Decklagen Beschichtung Randausführungen Einbauten Abhängsysteme Musterpaneele Anwendungen Fahrzeugbau Maschinenbau Kabinenbau Schienenfahrzeugbau Schiffsbau Flugzeugbau Architektur Kunst Tripan Cube Entwicklungsprojekte Unternehmen Philosophie Team Zertifizierungen Stellenangebote Downloads Kontakt Leichtbau Dienstleistungen Kernmaterialien Decklagen Beschichtung Randausführungen Einbauten Abhängsysteme Musterpaneele Anwendungen Fahrzeugbau Maschinenbau Kabinenbau Schienenfahrzeugbau Schiffsbau Flugzeugbau Architektur Kunst Tripan Cube Entwicklungsprojekte Unternehmen Philosophie Team Zertifizierungen Stellenangebote Downloads Kontakt de en JETZT PANEEL KONFIGURIEREN Design und Technologie perfekt vereint Leichtbauteile für den Fahrzeugbau Leichtbauteile für die Architektur Leichtbauteile für den Maschinenbau Leichtbauteile für den Kabinenbau MADE IN AUSTRIA PANEELE Ultraleicht und extrem stabil JETZT PANEEL KONFIGURIEREN DER SPEZIALIST FÜR INDIVIDUELLE LEICHTBAUTEILE Als Spezialist in der Leichtbau-Industrie ist TRIPAN bereits seit über 25 Jahren verlässlicher Partner für alle Paneel-Lösungen. Flexibles Oberflächendesign in Verbindung mit extrem belastbarer Innenstruktur – das zeichnet den Leichtbauteile-Hersteller TRIPAN aus. Der oberösterreichische Pionier für innovative Leichtbaulösungen kreiert individuelle Paneele für den modernen Alltag. Diese werden für die unterschiedlichsten Bedürfnisse und Anwendungen maßgeschneidert. Ultraleicht und extrem stabil in der Anwendung: Das ist die oberste Maxime der Produktentwicklung. Daher wird die zuverlässig hohe Qualität der Leichtbauteile von TRIPAN im Maschinen- und Fahrzeugbau genauso geschätzt wie im Flugzeug-, Kabinen-, Schienenfahrzeug- und Schiffsbau oder in der Architektur. Bionik im Fokus: Aluminium-Wabenkern bei Leichtbauteilen Die Bionik – von der Natur abschauen und systematisch weiterentwickeln – ist für die Leichtbau-Firma aus Oberösterreich ein wichtiger Aspekt. Daher wurde der Aluminium-Wabenkern in die TRIPAN-Verbundbauteile integriert. Dieser sorgt für hohe Belastbarkeit bei geringem Eigengewicht und erspart aufwendige Unterkonstruktionen. Zudem bietet er viel Platz für ein funktionelles Innenleben – von der Elektrik bis zur Wärme- und Schalldämmung. TRIPAN-Verbundbauteile bestehen aus einem druckfesten Wabenkern aus Aluminium oder Hartschaum und Decklagen aus Aluminium, Stahl oder Kunststoff. Produziert wird, was tatsächlich gebraucht wird – ganz nach unserem Motto „Create your panel“. Jedes Paneel erfüllt mehrere Funktionen: Es schützt, trägt und schafft Raum. Paneele mit einem Aluminium-Wabenkern sind druck- und biegefest, während sich Paneele mit einem Hartschaumkern durch hohe Wärmedämm­eigenschaften auszeichnen. Kundenspezifische Leichtbauteile für die Industrie Überall dort, wo geringes Eigengewicht zugunsten von hoher Nutzlast von Vorteil ist und wo geringe Masse Kraft spart, sind Leichtbauteile die ideale Lösung. Die optimale Auswahl der Werkstoffe und Komponenten ist der Qualitätsanspruch vom Leichtbauteile-Hersteller TRIPAN und basiert auf intensiver Forschung und langjähriger Erfahrung. Auf Wunsch erstellt TRIPAN das technische Gesamtkonzept von der Konstruktion über den Materialaufbau bis zum Prototyp und plant die Details der Endfertigung. Die detaillierte Ausführung als auch die Gestaltung der Abschlüsse und Kanten der Leichtbauteile werden von TRIPAN auf den Kundenbedarf abgestimmt und individuell gefertigt. Leichtbauteile vom Hersteller aus Oberösterreich TRIPAN ist ein international agierendes Unternehmen. Die Produktion am Standort Hörsching in Oberösterreich ist fixer Bestandteil der Firmenphilosophie. Heimische Wertschöpfung gepaart mit heimischer Handwerksqualität bildet das Fundament, auf dem das Unternehmen steht. Am Anfang steht eine Idee, eine neue Herausforderung – noch vage formuliert oder bereits in erste Pläne gefasst. Gemeinsam mit den Kunden entwickeln die Leichtbau-Spezialisten von TRIPAN das optimale Produkt. Mehr erfahren Nachhaltige und effiziente Lösungen Partikelschäume erfüllen unterschiedliche Aufgaben in unserem Alltag. Hätten Sie gedacht, dass diese so vielfältig sind? Mehr erfahren Lösungen Technische Formteile Bauindustrie Heizung / Sanitär Verpackung Kühllogistik / Catering Zuschnitte STYROPOR® NACHHALTIGER ALS PAPIER Lebenszyklusanalysen zeigen, dass EPS (Styropor ® | airpop ® ) deutlich geringere Auswirkungen auf die Umwelt hat, als andere, für den gleichen Zweck genutzte Materialien - insbesondere geringer als Papier. Polystyrolprodukte benötigen bei ihrer Herstellung mit Abstand weniger Ressourcen als Papier: Land, Wasser, Energie. ABFALLPROBLEM UNABHÄNGIG VOM MATERIAL Eine unsachgemäße Müllentsorgung trägt zu Abfallproblemen bei, unabhängig davon, ob es sich um EPS oder ein anderes Material handelt. Werden Abfälle jeglicher Art ordnungsgemäß in dem richtigen Müllbehältnis entsorgt, landet er nicht in der Umwelt. Styropor® kann recycelt oder thermisch verwertet werden, wenn dieser korrekt entsorgt wird. Nachhaltigkeit STYROPOR® ALTERNATIVEN MEIST TEURER Die Umweltkosten zeigen, dass Alternativen zu Kunststoffen 4 bis 5 mal mehr kosten. Denn Fleisch, Fisch und Produkte, die in EPS versandt und transportiert werden, haben eine längere Haltbarkeit, was zu weniger Lebensmittelsbfällen führt. Zudem schützt Styropor ® hochwertige Produkte, wie Elektrogeräte vor Schäden und Bruch. STYRPOR® ZU 100% RECYCLEBAR EPS ist zu 100% recyclingfähig und kann ein zweites Leben als neues Produkt, z.B. Surfboard, Lineal, Bilderrahmen oder Deckenzierleiste erhalten. Schon heute liegt die Recyclingquote für Styropor® über 50%. Neben der Möglichkeit EPS zu recyceln, kann der Partikelschaum ebenso thermisch verwertet werden und generiert so Energie zur Einsparung von Heizöl. text: Loyez Woessen – Loyez Woessen Loyez Woessen – Loyez Woessen LW 01062022 The French BUTTER company Branded and private label specialist Parc d'activités - Rue St. Patrick 59133 Phalempin - FRANCE +33 (0)3 20 90 55 00 contact@loyezwoessen.com Follow us on Linkedin Home Who we are Who we are Quality Policy Sustainability All Our Clients News All Our Events All Our Brands Butter Packs Conventional Butter Farmhouse Shapes Artisanale Farmhouse Shape Conventional Butter Artisanale Farmhouse shape Bio Butter Rolls Conventional Butter Butter Carton Pot Conventional Butter Reduced Fat Butter (60%) Butter with reduced fat content (60%) Conventional Our Formats, Your Possibilities Contact Us Export Locations Experience, Traditions since 1922 Experience, traditions is who we are since 1922 At the heart of the European dairy basin, our plant is strategically located to receive the raw material, and to export our quality finished goods. The company LOYEZ WOESSEN was founded in 1922 and specializes in the packaging and distribution of premium quality european butter. It started with the merger of two-family companies in the North of France. We are proud of our 100 years of long experience ! LOYEZ WOESSEN occupies a leading position in the butter sector while staying customer focused. It is my personal commitment to deliver the best quality product and service to our customers. Our competitive advantages High Service Level: >99,5% Quality stability Specific process (texture & spreadabilty) Availability, adaptability and quick feedback Strategic location (Northern France) Our Brands All Our Brands Butter Packs Conventional Butter Artisanale Farmhouse Shape Conventional Butter Bio Butter Rolls Conventional Butter Carton Pot Conventional Butter Butter with reduced fat content (60%) Conventional Butter Our Formats, Your Possibilities Contact Us Quality Policy Sustainability Thanks to our technological mastery and compliance with the strictest European hygiene and quality control standards, LOYEZ WOESSEN is a reliable and efficient supplier to its partners. Throughout the production, at every step, each employee is involved with the quality of our product. The quality management system has always been at the heart of our company's strategy. Its objective is the satisfaction of its customers. Because the quality of our products depends, above all, on the quality of our raw material, LOYEZ WOESSEN is very attentive to its origin. To obtain good butter, cows have access to pasture as soon as the climate allows it. Our suppliers limit the number of animals on their farm and focus on animal welfare. The organic farming certification, obtained in 2018, adds to this direction. They guarantee feed mainly composed of grasses and fodder. This certification is part of a sustainable development approach. Dysponujemy rozbudowanym parkiem maszynowym i stosujemy nowoczesne technologie – przekłada się to na wysoki standard wszystkich naszych usług. Obróbką metali zajmuje się u nas zespół fachowców z szeroką wiedzą i wieloletnim doświadczeniem. Naszym priorytetem jest dostarczanie klientom wyrobów zgodnych z ich indywidualnymi oczekiwaniami. Dzięki doskonałemu zapleczu technicznemu jesteśmy w stanie podjąć się nawet najbardziej nietypowych zleceń. Klientom zapewniamy kompleksową obsługę – zajmujemy się m.in. spawaniem stali . Posiadamy niezbędne certyfikaty umożliwiające świadczenie usług z zakresu obróbki konstrukcji stalowych . Wytwarzamy elementy wycinane zgodne z normą EN 1090-1, w związku z czym kwalifikują się do nadania znaku CE. Obsługujemy klientów z Polski, a także innych państw europejskich. Jakie metody obróbki blach stosujemy? Jednym z głównych obszarów naszej działalności jest obróbka blach . Stosujemy różnorodne metody, każdorazowo dopasowane do oczekiwanego efektu końcowego oraz gatunku i właściwości danego materiału. Specjalizujemy się zwłaszcza w cięciu laserowym , jednak stosujemy również wiele innych technologii, w tym plazmową i wodną. Klienci korzystający z naszych usług spawania konstrukcji stalowych czy też obróbki blachy otrzymują wyroby najwyższej jakości. Ponadto dbamy także o jak najszybszą realizację każdego zlecenia. Die Horitschoner Werzkeugbau GmbH ist ein mittelständisches Unternehmen im Osten Österreichs, gegründet 1994. An unserem Standort in Horitschon bieten wir mit 30 qualifizierten Mitarbeitern eine breite Palette an Leistungen um den Kunststoffspritzguss und mechanischer Fertigung an. Qualität, Made in Austria, Termintreue steht für uns an erster Stelle, ein Unternehmen mit Handschlagqualität! Kernkompetenzen unseres Unternehmens Konstruktion und Entwicklung von Kunststoffspritzgussformen für Branchen wie Automotive – E-Mobilität – Elektronik – Haushalt – Verpackung – Sonstiges Moldflowanalysen mit Verzugsvorhaltung, Einlegeteilen, etc. Artikeloptimierung bzw. Unser über 25 köpfiges Werkzeugbau - Team arbeitet im 2 Schichtbetrieb mit modernsten Maschinen, hochpräzise, um qualitativ hochwertige Spritzgussformen 100% Made in Austria zu fertigen.
